info.title: Foresignal API
info.summary: Headless intelligence broker: ingest, version and re-serve public telemetry.
info.description:
All configuration is done through this API. The MCP server is at `/mcp` (MCP streamable HTTP, protocol versions 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25) and is not an OpenAPI operation; it exposes the same data, the alert lifecycle and watch management as MCP tools, resources (`foresignal://sources`, `foresignal://kinds`) and the `situation-report` prompt (025, docs/Agent-Guide.md), plus the cost-bearing `search` tool (027) and the briefing tools `list_briefings`, `get_briefing_run`, `get_digest` (read), `create_briefing` and the cost-bearing `run_briefing` (agent) (029). It takes the same bearer tokens: `/mcp/**` needs `read` (open while `openReads` is on), tools are listed by the caller's scope and each checks its own (`read` tools; `agent` for writes such as `create_watch` and `set_alert_status`; cost-bearing tools always need a token), a session is bound to the token that opened it, and every tool call is audited (argument names only). The older HTTP+SSE transport (protocol 2024-11-05) is served at `/mcp/sse` with messages at `/mcp/message` only when `foresignal.mcp.legacy-sse.enabled=true`, for older clients. `GET /v1/system` reports its state under `mcp`. Reads of data are open on the local network; all writes and settings reads require the admin bearer token printed on first start. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json. Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC. `/v1` is additive-only once released.

**Key-in-path carriers.** Header-less clients use keys in the path: feed keys (`fsf_`, 035) as `/v1/k/{key}/<any allowed GET/HEAD path>`, tile keys (`fsk_`, 050) as `/v1/k/{key}/products/...`, `/v1/k/{key}/tiles/...`, `/v1/k/{key}/map/...` and `/v1/k/{key}/changes/stream` for map clients (MapLibre, maplibre_gl, Cesium, `EventSource`), share links (`fss_`, 112) as `/v1/k/{key}`. These are transports for the documented operations, not separate operations. A feed key reaches only `GET`/`HEAD` of `read` operations that are not always-authenticated, under the key's path prefixes, with the key's mandatory read restriction (unknown key 401 INVALID_FEED_KEY, expired or revoked 410 FEED_KEY_GONE, another method 405, a path outside the prefixes 403 RESTRICTED). A tile key reaches the same operations under its prefixes (a subset of `/v1/products/`, `/v1/styles`, `/v1/media/`, `/v1/tiles/`, `/v1/maps/static`, `/v1/sample`, `/v1/ground-stations/`, `/v1/changes/stream`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/v1/map/`), with its optional restriction and never private sources (unknown, expired or revoked key 401 INVALID_TILE_KEY, another method 405, a path outside the prefixes 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE). Responses carry `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; `Cache-Control` defaults to `private`, and a tile-key response takes the canonical path's own rule (`public` only while `openReads` covers it). Logs show only the key's first eight characters; the key is never echoed except by `createFeedKey` and `createTileKey`, and in the follow-up URLs of documents requested through it (058: the MapLibre style's sources and sprite, KML NetworkLink and icon hrefs, a feed's own `rel="self"` / `feed_url`), which are then always `Cache-Control: private`. CORS exposes `Foresignal-Frame-Time`, `Foresignal-Image-Bounds`, `Foresignal-Frame-Expired`, `Retry-After`, `Link` and `ETag`, allows `Authorization`, `If-None-Match` and `Foresignal-Prefetch`, and caches preflights for a day; `?prefetch=1` marks a render prefetch without the preflight the header causes.

**Restrictions and limits (035).** Restricted tokens, feed keys and the anonymous profile (`security.anonymous`, applied to tokenless reads while `openReads` is on) see only records and alerts inside their `ReadRestriction` on every read path (records, history, versions, changes, kinds, tiles, streams, search, alerts, the inbox, the digest, briefings, MCP tools and Ask): request filters are intersected with the restriction, and a single record or alert outside it is 404. Every client is rate-limited per class (`RateLimitSettings`); over a limit, or after repeated failed credentials from one address, the answer is 429 RATE_LIMITED with `Retry-After`. Device ingest URLs (039) and signed action links (033) use their own documented paths.

**Permissions (R2-004).** An operation a signed-in user needs a permission for carries `x-foresignal-permission`, a key of the `GET /v1/permissions` catalog (`users.manage`, `data.read`, `audit.read`…). A session bearer (`fss_`) is gated by that permission alone, in place of the scope: a user whose roles lack it gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with `requiredPermission`. An operation may list `x-foresignal-permission-alternatives`, further keys any one of which satisfies it as well (R2-009: the channel operations take `self.channels` or `channels.global`). An operation without one is gated on the session's derived scope. API tokens are gated by `x-foresignal-scope` only, as before: machines are not permission-scoped, so an `admin` token satisfies every permission and a lower token gets 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.

**Status annotations.** Every operation has `x-foresignal-prompt` (the build prompt that implements it), optional `x-foresignal-extended-by`, and `x-foresignal-status` (`planned` until implemented). Clients can mock the whole API from this document and filter by status.

**Outside this document:** the MCP server (`/mcp`, plus the legacy SSE transport when enabled), Actuator endpoints (`/actuator/**`), and sink listeners on their own ports (110).

x-foresignal-changelog.note: 160: getCollectorStatus (GET /v1/settings/collector/status, admin) with the CollectorStatus schema: the pull governor's live cap, inUse and waiting, so the admin app's collector screen can show the governor working, not only its maxConcurrentPulls setting. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed; part of the 1.3.0 wave, no version change.

158: relationship intelligence for people and organizations (model and queries only). The canonical entity resolver and relation graph, physical-domain only until now (aircraft / vessel / satellite / station), gain person and organization entity types and the corporate / person identity keys that resolve them deterministically: lei, company-number (JURISDICTION:NUMBER), tax-id and officer-id (REGISTRY:ID) are anchors for organizations, and person-key (a normalized name key) is a weak key for people — added to the EntityKey, EntityKeyInput and EntityLink keyType enums and the Entity type enum. Five ownership / affiliation relation types join the vocabulary — owns, controls, officer-of, beneficial-owner, affiliated-with — usable on createRelation, listRelatedObjects and queryGraph. A new ownershipChain query (POST /v1/graph/ownership-chain, read) is the sibling of findCommonDependencies: it walks those edges from up to 50 seed entities and returns each reached entity's strongest, shortest chain, with the subset reached from two or more seeds surfaced as a shared attribute (a common owner, officer, address or affiliate). This builds the model and queries; the external corporate / UBO / PEP / leak data that populates the edges is deferred to the Future-Roadmap. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

157: author-able correlation recipes, shared-attribute joins, settings-driven thresholds. An operator can now author a correlation recipe through the API, not only toggle a bundled one: createRecipe (POST /v1/intel/recipes, admin) persists a validated operator-authored recipe beside the bundled classpath recipes (new CorrelationRecipeCreate schema), and updateRecipe additionally accepts a full definition to replace for an operator recipe (CorrelationRecipeUpdate gains definition); a bundled recipe's definition stays managed by the classpath. CorrelationRecipe gains origin (bundled / operator). A recipe join gains a sharedAttribute predicate — a candidate joins when its payload value at a dot-path equals a seed member's (an address, phone, officer or shared id), matching on the attribute alone without geometry — the foundation for fraud/relationship recipes (pairing with 158's ownership edges). The Admiralty reliability numbers and the coverage skew/blindspot thresholds are now settings (media.reliabilityNumbers, news.coverageThresholds), mirroring media.reliabilityMap, so the admin app can tune them. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

156: probabilistic threshold-crossing forecaster. A "will this series cross X by date Y" binary question (a series-value or count-threshold resolver with an op and threshold over a series) is now answered from a numeric predictive distribution instead of a flat confidence: a new threshold forecaster reads P(value op threshold) off the implied CDF of the numeric forecaster's quantiles for the resolution window — the ensemble pool of the climatology baseline and the statistical series forecast (ETS today, an external quantile forecaster such as TimesFM tomorrow), falling back to whichever is available. The persistence forecaster no longer contributes its flat confidence to these questions (numeric series-value carry-forward and situation-status are unchanged). Surfaced through the existing forecast endpoints; threshold is added to the forecaster-type enums. Part of the 1.3.0 wave; no version change.

155: on-demand external forecaster round-trip. A first-class external forecaster (a model like TimesFM) can now be asked to forecast a specific ledger question on demand: the EDP manifest gains an optional transport.analysisRequest endpoint (EdpAnalysisRequest schema), and requestAnalysis (POST /v1/external/analysis/requests) posts {questionId, horizon, correlationId, callbackUrl} to it and persists the correlation. The provider answers synchronously in the response and/or asynchronously to analysisCallback (POST /v1/external/analysis/callback), which resolves the correlation and records the forecast through the usual binding path as the external forecaster edp:{sourceId}/{streamId}. createForecastEvaluation can now backtest a type=external forecaster by issuing as-of analysis requests (previously skipped). An operator can pre-register, name and configure an external forecaster independent of the auto-derived id with registerExternalForecaster (POST /v1/forecasts/forecasters, ExternalForecasterRegistration schema); ForecasterUpdate gains an optional name, and a per-forecaster externalMinResolved config overrides the ensemble default. A decile-only provider (p10..p90, as TimesFM emits) is accepted and mapped binding-side onto the ledger's required quantiles (p05/p25/p50/p75/p95) without loosening the required set. TimesFM stays an external Python service; no Python enters the backend. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

154: timely corroboration. The hardcoded "promote to a trusted signal" gates are now the tunable corroboration policy: adds getIntelCorroboration (GET /v1/intel/corroboration) and updateIntelCorroboration (PUT, admin) with the IntelCorroboration schema — event evidence-quality thresholds (strongFamilies / strongGroups / moderateFamilies), a situation activation rule (minFamilies / minGroups), and the automatic corroboration of lone events (enabled, withinKm, window, maxMembers). A sensing modality (sensor / imagery / official / social / media / crowd / operator / derived), derived from the originator class, is now a distinct independence dimension: eventQuality.requireModalities and a recipe's activateAt.modalities require a candidate to span several modalities before it is strong or active. A lone agent/analyst/operator event now searches for independent corroborating records near it in space and time on creation and auto-activates once independent evidence groups accumulate. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

153: de-hype & partisan vetting. Claim gains a neutral restatement (the de-hyped who/what/where/when core, an LLM proposal kept only when it re-validates against the lexicon, gazetteer and entity index, otherwise synthesized deterministically), a deterministic LLM-free framingScore with a framingLabel band (neutral / charged / inflammatory) measuring how the most central post is told rather than whether it is true, and a reputation member (new ClaimReputation schema: outlet factuality, lean, state-affiliation) when the source resolves to a rated outlet — folded into sourceReliability as news reliability already grades news. The claim-extraction-system prompt template is now 1.1.0 (it emits the restatement while staying an extractor, never an arbiter); 1.0.0 stays bundled. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

152: numeric / quantile forecast calibration. getForecastCalibration now returns a numeric calibration for a numeric-only forecaster or question — a quantile-reliability diagram (empirical coverage of each stated quantile vs its nominal level), a PIT histogram and a calibration-error summary (new ForecastNumericCalibration schema, type: numeric) — and the binary CORP/bins calibration otherwise (unchanged). The 200 response is now oneOf [ForecastCalibration, ForecastNumericCalibration]. Part of the 1.3.0 wave; no version change.

151: signal calibration. Confidence is reported as a calibrated probability where enough real-world outcomes have resolved, otherwise the raw EventScorer score unchanged; IntelligenceEvent and IntelEventSummary gain rawConfidence, confidence is no longer capped at 0.95 when calibrated, and the calibrated flag now means a fitted mapping was applied (not 103 validation). Adds getIntelCalibration (GET /v1/intel/calibration) and getIntelCalibrationScope (GET /v1/intel/calibration/{scope}) with the IntelCalibration schema (reliability table, Brier, sample size, CORP curve). The intel SSE topic gains intel.event.upgraded, emitted alongside intel.event.updated when a change crosses a trust threshold (status emerging→active, a confidence or evidence-quality tier, uncorroborated→corroborated, or calibrated turning true); its summary carries an upgrade member. Additive: no operation or schema was renamed or removed.

150: minor bump for two additive operations: getCollectorSettings and updateCollectorSettings (GET/PUT /v1/settings/collector, schema CollectorSettings: maxConcurrentPulls, the size of the global pull governor), and enableCoreSources (POST /v1/sources/enable-core, schema EnableCoreSourcesResult). A fresh install now seeds only the core set enabled; enableFreeSources is unchanged and its description now says so.

148: documentation only. enableFreeSources and EnableFreeSourcesResult.skipped now say that a source held off by default (wiki-edit-surge, prompt 146) is skipped. No operation, schema or parameter changed.

146: info.version is 1.1.0, the minor bump for enableFreeSources (145), which is additive against the frozen v1.0.0 contract. No operation, schema or parameter changed in 146; wiki-edit-surge now seeds disabled and is skipped by enableFreeSources (a free source held off for its bandwidth).

145: free sources are enabled by default. A built-in source that runs without operator input (no required credential, no required parameter, parameters valid with nothing supplied) is seeded enabled; credential- or parameter-gated sources are still seeded disabled. Adds enableFreeSources (POST /v1/sources/enable-free, admin) and the EnableFreeSourcesResult schema, which bring an existing install to that default in one idempotent call. Additive: no operation or schema is changed or removed.

144: release 1.0.0. info.version is reset from the pre-release document version 1.3.0 to the product release 1.0.0, and this document is frozen at docs/api/v1.0.0/OpenAPI.json. From here /v1 is additive only (NFR-10): checkApiCompat runs oasdiff breaking against the frozen copy, and breaking changes go to /v2. No operation, schema or parameter changed in 144.

098: the seven entity operations (listEntities, resolveEntity, getEntity, listEntityRecords, addEntityKey, retractEntityKey, mergeEntities) are implemented with the Entity, EntityKey, EntityAlias, EntityLink, EntityPage, EntityRecordList, EntityKeyInput and EntityMergeInput schemas, the ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, ENTITY_KEY_INVALID and ENTITY_KEY_CONFLICT codes and AccessPolicy rules (reads read, writes admin). The new source faa-registry (aircraft-registration, US-PD, no owner PII) and the new record sources; WatchlistInput.identity gains entity (an entity:<ULID> item expands to the entity's open keys). No operation was renamed or removed.

096: no new operations. New sources stac-sentinel2 (sentinel-2-c1-l2a), stac-landsat (landsat-c2-l2) and stac-sentinel1 (sentinel-1-grd, disabled by default), all kind satellite-scene, each requiring an aoi (bbox or place id). Record x-foresignal-kinds fills in the satellite-scene payload; the record also carries title and eventTime (the tile property list reads them). Foresignal never downloads, proxies or signs an imagery asset: records carry the STAC item link and, only for an https thumbnail, the thumbnail URL.

092: no new operations. New sources cloudflare-radar-outages (kind internet-outage), cloudflare-radar-bgp (kinds bgp-hijack, bgp-leak), ripe-atlas-probes (kind probe-status), gpsjam-daily (kind jamming-cell, disabled by default), the status-* Statuspage family and status-gcp/status-google-workspace (kinds service-status, service-incident), and the status-aws/status-azure feed-kit entries. The feed-kit id pattern now admits the reviewed status- prefix.

091: no new operations. x-foresignal-kinds fills in the sanction payload (ofac-sdn, uk-sanctions-list, un-sanctions) and filing (sec-8k) notes. The UK source is now uk-sanctions-list (the FCDO UK Sanctions List), replacing the closed OFSI list. The descriptor User-Agent may carry a contact suffix (`; contact=…`); it is not a separate schema property.

090: no new operations. The descriptor schema's llmNotice field is now served (a per-source notice appended whenever its records reach an LLM context; OpenFEMA sets it). x-foresignal-kinds fills in the payloads and notes for natural-event (nasa-eonet), disaster (reliefweb-disasters), displacement (unhcr-population), disease-outbreak (who-don), emergency-activation (copernicus-ems), volcano-alert (usgs-hans-volcanoes, geonet-volcanoes), disaster-declaration (openfema-declarations) and travel-advisory (travel-advisory-us).

089: no new operations. Record x-foresignal-kinds gains cap-alert, rainfall-outlook, earthquake-impact and shakemap-mmi, for the reviewed cap-* family and the meteoalarm-* family, the five WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook feature-kit sources (wpc-ero-d1..d5), emsc-seismic (kind earthquake), the fdsn-* services (kind earthquake) and usgs-shakemap. The earthquake kind gains the emsc-seismic and fdsn-* payloads (mag, magType, place, depthKm, auth, sourceCatalog, evtype; depth is in the payload, the point is 2D).
Complete target API for prompts 006-144 authored up front (API-first), including social signals (135-137) and the External Data Protocol (024, 138).
008: IngestOutcome.rejections[].reason lists the normalizer's rejection codes (description only; no schema change).
009: IngestOutcome byReason, live and touched descriptions state their exact meaning (description only; no schema change).
010: probeSource documents 409 NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_MODE for push and derived sources, which have no upstream to probe.

013: every Sources operation of prompt 013 (including listSourceFetches) is implemented; updateSource's 400 attributes INGEST_POLICY_INVALID and RETENTION_TIER_FIXED to 013 (was 014, a pre-v1.3 number); SourceDescriptor.defaultIngestPolicy documents that the §5.1 defaults are filled in (description only).

014: listRecords, getRecord, listRecordVersions, queryHistory, listKinds, getKindSchema and listChanges are implemented. Feature.properties gains ingestedAt and persistReason for version-based features (history, asOf); KindSchema documents x-datum, the TIMESTAMP mapping and per-variant x-sources; ChangePage.lastSeq documents that an exhausted page advances to the watermark; the change-feed geojsonseq Feature carries the Change fields as properties (descriptions and optional properties only; no operation changed).

015: streamChanges, streamEvents and updateEventStreamFilter are implemented. streamChanges' 429 is the per-principal STREAM_LIMIT (was described as RATE_LIMITED); streamChanges and streamEvents document 404 for an unknown source in the filter (the behavior of the 014 read endpoints), and updateEventStreamFilter's 404 covers it too (responses only; no parameter or schema changed).

016: getTile, listTileLayers and getTileJson are implemented. getTile's Cache-Control is max-age=5 for raw and max-age=60 for aggregated tiles (was described as max-age=300; 037 keeps the immutable form for closed asOf instants), its ETag is a hash of the tile bytes and Vary is documented; the getTile description documents the feature and cell properties, the half-open tile and cell assignment and hex cells straddling tile edges; listTileLayers lists layers with a source the caller can see (private sources for token callers) and leaves out kinds spelled like a source id (descriptions and response headers only; no parameter or schema changed).

017: listTriggers, getTrigger, createTrigger, updateTrigger, deleteTrigger, testTrigger, snoozeTrigger, unsnoozeTrigger, listAlerts, getAlert, streamAlerts, acknowledgeAlert, resolveAlert, snoozeAlert, unsnoozeAlert and setAlertFeedback are implemented, and the alerts topic of /v1/events/stream. Additive reconciliations: EventStreamAlertsFilter and streamEvents gain includeSuppressed (alerts.includeSuppressed); streamAlerts documents 400 INVALID_CURSOR and 404 for an unknown source; listAlerts, getAlert and streamAlerts hide alerts of private sources from anonymous callers; Near.point radiusKm minimum is 0.1 (was 0); TriggerRuleInput.geofence accepts geofenceRoute plus bufferMeters as the route input; Condition.op documents the type rules (string operators need a JSON string; a missing value or another type never matches) and the accepted regex subset; hysteresisMeters documents its semantics.

018: listChannelTypes, listChannels, createChannel, getChannel, updateChannel, deleteChannel, testChannel, listChannelDeliveries, getNotificationSettings and updateNotificationSettings are implemented, and the notifications (cursor key n) and system (cursor key s) topics of /v1/events/stream. Additive reconciliations: listChannelDeliveries documents 400 (invalid status, limit or cursor); ChannelInput.events documents that 018 accepts alert, briefing and system; ChannelInput.secrets and ChannelType.secretFields document the prefix.<Name> wildcard (webhook header.<Name>); Channel.secretFields lists the names of the secrets that are set; NotificationMessage.subtype lists alert.digest and system.rule_storm.

019: getRetention, updateRetention, runRetention, getCors, updateCors, exportSettings, importSettings, getSystem, rotateAdminToken, getWatchdogSettings and updateWatchdogSettings are implemented. Additive reconciliations: RetentionSettings.notifications belongs to 019 (notification rows; the inbox is 033's `inbox`), its description states the resolution order and that later members are accepted and not stored; SettingsBundle.channels items carry the channel id (ChannelInput plus id) because import upserts by id; SettingsBundle.triggers documents that ids are kept.

020: getOpenApiDocument is implemented (served by a controller, byte-identical to docs/OpenAPI.json), and the notification and watchdogHeartbeat webhooks are marked implemented (018, 019). Additive reconciliations: every SSE operation's text/event-stream schema is an anyOf of the event schemas named in x-foresignal-sse-events (was a bare string; anyOf because the SSE event name, not the data, selects the schema); every webhook operation declares security [] (outbound; the receiver authenticates it by the documented signature); getOpenApiDocument, getSystem, getVapidPublicKey, getJwks, getSystemJwks and getEdpProtocol document a 4XX problem response, as the lint requires. Alert.ruleName is nullable (null once the rule is deleted, as 017 implements). streamAlerts' alert.enriched event carries prompt 030, like the same event on streamEvents.

022: streamEvents' canonical.created, canonical.merged and canonical.flagged events carry topic evidence and prompt 116, like the other later-prompt events (they were ungated, so the conformance test counted them as current). Additive; no operation or schema changed.

023: listTokens, createToken, revokeToken, getSecuritySettings, updateSecuritySettings, getServerSettings, updateServerSettings, createStreamTicket, updateCurrentTokenDevice, listPairingCodes, createPairingCode, deletePairingCode, getPairingCodeQr, claimPairingCode and listAuditEvents are implemented. Additive reconciliations: Problem documents requiredScope (INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE) and lists the codes INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, ENDPOINT_NOT_ALLOWED, RESTRICTION_NOT_ENFORCED (403), BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN (409), PAIRING_CODE_INVALID (400) and RATE_LIMITED (429); getSystem's full document needs at least the read scope; updateSecuritySettings refuses the 035/069 members until those prompts; updateServerSettings requires publicBaseUrl (null allowed), restricts clientLinks templates to foresignal:// and https://, refuses push until 031 and documents PUBLIC_BASE_URL_MISMATCH; createToken documents the bbox rule and refuses restriction members and privateAccess that later prompts enforce; getPairingCodeQr is available until a restart.

024: the custom-source, ingest, ntfy/Gotify compatibility and External Data Protocol operations are implemented (listCustomSources, createCustomSource, getCustomSource, updateCustomSource, deleteCustomSource, rotateIngestKey, ingestRecords, ingestRecordsFormat, ingestWebhookHandshake, listIngestFormats, ntfyPublish, ntfyPublishPut, ntfyPublishViaGet, ntfyPublishViaPost, ntfyPublishJson, gotifyPublish, getEdpProtocol, getEdpSchema, listExternalSources, registerExternalSource, getExternalSource, deleteExternalSource, updateExternalSourceManifest, approveExternalSource, suspendExternalSource, pushExternalItems, listRegistrationTokens, createRegistrationToken, deleteRegistrationToken, selfRegisterExternalSource, validateEdp). Reconciliations: pushExternalItems and updateExternalSourceManifest take x-foresignal-scope `open` with the ingest-key schemes, like ingestRecords (an ingest key of the source, or an admin token), instead of `agent`; ExternalSourceRegistration gains allowPrivateNetwork (EDP §7 per-source permission) and ExternalSource gains allowPrivateNetwork, presentation and breakingChanges; CustomSourceFormats.mapping accepts the 024 JSON-Pointer IngestRecordMapping (new schema) alongside 059's RecordMapping; createCustomSource refuses the members later prompts enforce; an admin token is not asked for a sender signature; manifest updates that change provider URLs, update styles or geometry types also return a source to pending; Problem lists SOURCE_EXISTS, KIND_IN_USE, OBSERVED_AT_MODE_LOCKED, INGEST_RECORD_RATE, FORMAT_UNKNOWN, SIGNATURE_INVALID, SOURCE_DISABLED, INGEST_BUSY, MANIFEST_INVALID, PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED, SOURCE_MISMATCH, SOURCE_PENDING_APPROVAL, SOURCE_SUSPENDED, REGISTRATION_TOKEN_INVALID, SOURCE_ID_NOT_ALLOWED and UNKNOWN_EXTERNAL_SOURCE; ingestRecordsFormat's JSON body also admits any JSON document, which the `mapping` format reads; the outbound edpProviderItems call is implemented (the pull adapter), and edpProviderSearch is re-assigned to 137, whose cue service makes the call (024 stores transport.search); new operation allowExternalSnapshot (POST /v1/external/sources/{sourceId}/snapshots/{snapshotId}/allow, admin) releases a snapshot deletion held above maxAbsentRatio once, the operator control EDP §3.2 describes.

025: the MCP server is built. It owns no OpenAPI operation; info.description now documents /mcp (streamable HTTP; tools listed and checked by scope, cost-bearing tools always authenticated, sessions bound to their token, per-call audit with argument names only) and the optional legacy HTTP+SSE transport at /mcp/sse and /mcp/message (foresignal.mcp.legacy-sse.enabled). getSystem's full document now carries SystemInfo.mcp (enabled, transports.streamable, transports.legacySse, sessions, tools) and features.mcp, as already specified.

026: listLlmProviders, createLlmProvider, getLlmProvider, updateLlmProvider, deleteLlmProvider, testLlmProvider, listLlmProviderModels, getLlmSettings, updateLlmSettings and getLlmUsage are implemented. Additive reconciliations: LlmProviderInput.options gains `local` (the flag LlmProvider.local already referred to) and documents the temperature range (refused for anthropic) and the reserved extraHeaders; createLlmProvider documents the type defaults and that anthropic needs an apiKey; updateLlmProvider requires a body id to match the path and refuses a change that leaves an assigned role unserved; testLlmProvider reports provider failures and refusals in the result (200) and only budget refusals as 429; listLlmProviderModels documents 429 LLM_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED; updateLlmSettings replaces the setting and accepts allowPrivateLocal only as false until 039; Problem lists LLM_BUDGET_EXCEEDED (429), LLM_PROVIDER_EXISTS (409), LLM_PROVIDER_IN_USE (409), LLM_PROVIDER_ERROR (502) and LLM_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED (429). getSystem's full document carries SystemInfo.llm and features.llm; the SettingsBundle carries llmProviders (without keys) and llmSettings, as already specified.

027: search, getSearchStatus, reindexSearch and cancelReindex are implemented. Additive reconciliations: SearchResults gains an optional `reason` (why results degraded to text); search documents 404 for an unknown source or a private source the caller may not see, and that since/until apply to the timeField axis; SourceSettingsUpdate.embed documents that `true` is refused for a source without embedFields or a private one and that turning it off deletes the source's record documents; Problem lists REINDEX_RUNNING (409) and SEMANTIC_UNAVAILABLE (409). getSystem's full document carries SystemInfo.search and features.search / features.semanticSearch; the MCP server adds the cost-bearing `search` tool (info.description). SourceSettings.embed, SearchStatus.activeModel/reindex/degraded, SearchResult.seq/effectiveTime and the timeField/docType parameters were already specified.

028: ask, askStream, listAskThreads, getAskThread, deleteAskThread, confirmAskAction and rejectAskAction are implemented. Additive reconciliations: ask and askStream document 400 (unknown members, scope; scope.placeIds and scope.viewId are refused until prompt 036) and 404 (threadId of another caller); askStream's 429 also covers STREAM_LIMIT (per-principal Ask stream limit), and a budget refusal after the stream opened is an `error` event; listAskThreads and getAskThread are described as always authenticated, matching their x-foresignal-always-authenticated flag; confirmAskAction documents that a failed execution is returned as status `failed` with result.error (200); Problem lists LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED (409) and ACTION_NOT_PENDING (409). AskScope.placeIds, AskMessage.citations/warnings, the stream `warning` event and AskAction.type `alert_status` were already specified.

029: listBriefings, createBriefing, previewBriefing, getBriefing, updateBriefing, deleteBriefing, runBriefing, listBriefingRuns, getBriefingRun, getLatestBriefingRun and getDigest are implemented. A rule's area itself needs no new member: a country or admin-1 region is a geofenceRef, a place or circle is near.point with radiusKm, a polygon or box is a Polygon geofence, and a route is a LineString geofence with bufferMeters. A rule's area is tested against a record's geometry only, so a record without geometry never matches an area. analyzeTriggerSources is recorded as prompt 161 (it was tagged 017).

API 1.4.1 (a patch: contract corrections, nothing changed or removed). The log-action lists now say what the server writes and are declared x-extensible-enum, since they grow as the server adds actions: IntelEventLogEntry.action gains upgraded (the 151 trust-threshold crossing, written beside the update by an operator edit or by the correlation engine), SituationTimelineEntry.action gains edited (written by every updateSituation, beside any renamed, theme or severity entries), and NarrativeLogEntry.action is unchanged. A client must accept an action it does not know.

162: API 1.5.0 (additive, a minor version: nothing changed or removed). LLM provider setup for the admin app. probeLlmProvider (POST /v1/llm/probe, admin, always authenticated) tests an unsaved LlmProviderInput and lists its models in one round trip, persisting nothing (LlmProbeResult). LlmProviderInput and LlmProvider gain `pricing` (LlmPricing: input, output, cached-input and embedding USD per million tokens) and hourlyCapUsd, dailyCapUsd and monthlyCapUsd: USD caps on UTC hour, day and month boundaries, enforced against the provider's self-metered spend and refused 429 LLM_BUDGET_EXCEEDED with Retry-After at the window's reset, on top of requestsPerMinute and tokensPerDay. getLlmProviderBudget (GET /v1/llm/providers/{providerId}/budget, admin) reports spend, reservations, cap and remaining per window, the token limits, and the provider-reported balance for providers that expose one to the inference key (LlmProviderBudget, LlmSpendWindow, LlmProviderBalance). LlmUsagePoint gains costUsd.

API 2.0.0 (Release-2 platform contract, authored before implementation; every new operation is x-foresignal-status `planned` and tagged with its R2 implementation prompt R2-003..R2-027). Turns ForeSignal from a single-operator instance into a multi-user RBAC platform. New operations: email/password auth and sessions (/v1/auth/login|logout|password/reset-request|password/reset|activate, GET /v1/auth/sessions, DELETE /v1/auth/sessions and /v1/auth/sessions/{id}); user management (/v1/users CRUD plus roles, suspend, unsuspend, resend-invite, password-reset); roles and the permission catalog (/v1/roles CRUD, GET /v1/permissions); SMTP settings and test (/v1/settings/smtp, /v1/settings/smtp/test); per-user source views and the instance collection set (/v1/me/sources, /v1/sources/collection); the caller's LLM budget (/v1/me/llm/budget); preferences (/v1/me/preferences); host resource monitoring and thresholds (/v1/system/resources, /v1/settings/thresholds); a retention preview (/v1/settings/retention/preview); the cold-storage archival tier (/v1/archives, /v1/archives/run, /v1/archives/{id}/restore); backup and restore (/v1/settings/backup, /v1/backups, /v1/backups/run, /v1/backups/{id}/restore); egress routing and IP rotation (/v1/egress CRUD, test, health, /v1/settings/egress, PUT /v1/sources/{sourceId}/egress); first-party aggregators (/v1/aggregators, /v1/aggregators/{domain}, test); MFA (/v1/me/mfa/enroll|verify|disable, recovery-codes); user-owned API tokens (/v1/me/tokens); per-user quotas (/v1/users/{id}/quota, /v1/me/quota); and first-run onboarding (/v1/system/first-run, /v1/setup). Semantic change (no shape change): existing per-operator config becomes per-user owned (owner_user_id) — triggers, channels, personal LLM providers and saved views are the caller's own (an operator also manages shared/global entries), and a source's enablement/display is the caller's per-user view over the shared collection; the collection is still pulled once by the paced collector (the union of users' views). GET /v1/me additionally reflects the authenticated user and effective permissions. The move to 2.0.0 is the version at which these per-user semantics apply; the wire shapes of the affected operations are unchanged, so the additive-only check against the frozen v1.0.0 contract still passes. The GET/PUT /v1/settings/archive and /v1/settings/retention operations already existed (prompts 111 and 019) and are reused; /v1/archives is the new archival-tier inventory, distinct from the compliance cold-archive catalog (/v1/archive/catalog).

API 2.1.0 (Automated Newspaper). The contract was authored by NP-001 with every new operation x-foresignal-status `planned`; NP-002 to NP-006 implemented them and NP-007 activated them, so every operation of the feature is now `implemented`. Extends the briefing engine into per-user editions rather than adding a parallel subsystem. New operations: news translation settings (getTranslationSettings, updateTranslationSettings: GET/PUT /v1/settings/translation, admin); the caller's news subscriptions (getMyNewsSubscriptions, updateMyNewsSubscriptions: GET/PUT /v1/me/news-subscriptions, read, self.sources); the caller's editions (listMyEditions: GET /v1/me/editions, read); and the hosted edition site (getEditionSite: GET /v1/editions/{briefingId}/site, read, open while openReads is on, reachable by feed key and share link). Added while implementing (NP-004 to NP-006): BriefingRun.deliveryResults, the read-only outcome of each delivery target (NP-004); openEditionSiteShareLink (GET /v1/k/{key}/site, open: the hosted edition site through its share link) and the share-link target type `edition-site` (NP-005); and BriefingRun.breaking, the read-only alert that fired a breaking-news run (NP-006). New schemas: TranslationSettings, TranslationSettingsInput, NewsSubscription, NewsSubscriptionView, NewsSubscriptionUpdate, EditionSummary, EditionSite, DeliveryTarget, BreakingNewsConfig. Additive, optional fields: BriefingInput gains outputLanguage (NP-003), deliveryTargets (NP-004), site (NP-005), breakingNews (NP-006), includeProvenance and includeCorroboration (NP-007); Briefing gains the read-only ownerUserId (NP-003); AskCitation gains provenance and corroboration, set only on briefing-run citations of a briefing with the matching flag (NP-007); NewsArticle and NewsStory gain targetLanguage, translatedTitle, translatedExcerpt and translationProvenance beside the untouched originals (NP-002). No operation or schema was renamed or removed; a 2.0.0 client stays valid.

API 2.1.1 (newspaper editions: ownership + self-service). Additive. BriefingInput gains the writable ownerUserId: on createBriefing/updateBriefing it defaults to the creating user and only a caller holding users.manage may set it to another user, to assign an edition on their behalf; Briefing.ownerUserId stays read-only in responses. New self-service edition operations under /v1/me/editions let a signed-in user holding the new self.editions permission own and manage an edition without agent scope: createMyEdition (POST /v1/me/editions), updateMyEdition (PUT /v1/me/editions/{briefingId}), deleteMyEdition (DELETE /v1/me/editions/{briefingId}) and runMyEdition (POST /v1/me/editions/{briefingId}/run); ownerUserId is forced to the caller on these. No operation or schema was renamed or removed; a 2.1.0 client stays valid. Authored contract-first; implemented and activated by NP-008.

get.description:
Current state from record_head ⋈ record_live (merged payload, live geometry); expired and tombstoned records are excluded unless requested, and `watermarkSeq` is read before the query. Mirror contract: (1) open SSE with `after = watermarkSeq`, (2) page the snapshot with `order=id` (the cursor pins `asOfSeq ?? watermarkSeq`; later updates arrive via `/v1/changes?after=<w>`), (3) apply an event only if its observedAt ≥ the stored one. `asOf=T` replays transaction time and needs a source or kind filter (400 ASOF_FILTER_REQUIRED, ASOF_BEYOND_RETENTION with `horizon`, ASOF_INVALID).

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

get.description:
Mapbox Vector Tile of current live state (record_live ⋈ record_head): geometry and observedAt come from record_live, so a live position shows before any new version is persisted. `layer` is a source id (wins) or a kind declared by a visible source; anything else is 404 UNKNOWN_LAYER. Raw features carry `source`, `externalId`, `kind`, `title` (record_head.title), `observedAt` (epoch seconds, number), `version` (number), `live` (boolean, record_live.dirty) plus the layer sources' valid `tileProperties` (names matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$`) read from the merged payload with their native JSON types; null values are omitted. Raw tiles are capped at foresignal.tiles.maxFeatures (default 50,000) newest-first, with `Foresignal-Tile-Truncated: true` when the cap was hit. Aggregated tiles (`agg=grid|hex`, or `auto` below the layer's aggBelowZoom, which is the lowest value its visible sources declare) carry one polygon per non-empty cell with `count`, `latestObservedAt` (epoch seconds), `kinds` (a JSON string, kind → count), `agg` (`grid` or `hex`) and `maxRank` only when every source of the layer declares a numeric rankField. Cells are built in EPSG:3857 with foresignal.tiles.cellsPerTile (default 32) cells across a tile; grid cells line up with tile edges. Each record is reduced to ST_PointOnSurface (a polygon counts once) and counted in exactly one tile (half-open tile envelope) and one cell; a hex cell that straddles a tile edge is drawn by both tiles, each counting the records on its own side. Private sources never appear in features or counts for anonymous callers. An empty tile is 200 with an empty body. With `asOf` (037) the tile shows the layer as known at that instant (transaction axis, record_version): per entity the newest version with seq in [L, S(asOf)] that is not a tombstone, still inside the tile and valid at asOf (an entity that moved out is not drawn at its old position); raw features carry `source`, `externalId`, `kind`, `title` (from the version payload), `observedAt`, `version` and the tile properties, without `live`; the same cap and aggregation apply.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

post.description:
Asks the chat provider, through the versioned template `source-relevance-system@1.0.0` and the analyst purpose, how much each of 2 to 50 sources contributes to a dataset built from all of them, with a one-sentence reason per source. The model sees only catalog content, as an untrusted data block: each source's name, description, kinds and entity identity types, and the kinds and identity types two or more of them share (`shared`). The answer is advice: nothing is enabled, omitted or stored, and the caller decides which sources the rule keeps. Every requested source comes back exactly once, in request order. A source the egress policy keeps from the provider (a private source and a remote provider) is not sent and comes back `unrated`, as does one the model left out or rated with another value; when fewer than two sources may be sent, or the answer cannot be read, every source is `unrated` with the reason. Spends LLM budget, so it always needs a token.

**Scope:** `agent`.

post.summary: Push records in a named format
post.description:
Parses the body with the named `IngestFormat` and submits one batch to the single writer (same versioning, policies, live/touch semantics, change stream, triggers and retention as polled data). Credentials: `X-Foresignal-Ingest-Key`, `Authorization: Bearer eik_…`, Basic with the key as password, a device key (039, bound to one entity), or an `admin` token; a configured signature verifier must also pass unless `keyOptional`. 200 when the request is valid even with per-record rejections (MISSING_OBSERVED_AT, LOW_ACCURACY, …). OwnTracks, Overland, OsmAnd and GPSLogger get their native reply shapes; the device presets (059) reply as their firmware expects (ecowitt an empty 200, wu-pws `success`, gmc `OK.`). `Content-Encoding: gzip` is accepted (decompressed size capped at 5 MB → 413). The `same` format (086) reads one SAME header per line (multimon-ng `EAS: ZCZC-…` output or bare headers), ignores `NNNN`, collapses an identical header repeated within 10 s, and stores `same-alert` records on the named counties (the state's counties for `PSS000`) with `validUntil` = issue + purge. The `chirpstack-v4` format maps `?event=up`, moves the device on `?event=location`, acknowledges other events and refuses Protobuf (415). An `admin` token is the operator and is not asked for a sender signature.

**Scope:** ingest key (or an `admin` token).

Versions in [from, to] by seq (≤ 200,000 rows scanned, else `truncated`), POSITION_STALE carry-forwards skipped, new segment after a tombstone or a gap > `gap`, the live position appended when newer, Douglas–Peucker simplification keeping endpoints and FIRST/REAPPEAR/SIGNIFICANT/TRIGGER_EDGE points, split at the antimeridian. Window larger than the source's retention → 400 TRACK_WINDOW_TOO_LARGE. Caching as asOf tiles, keyed on `to`; a response with an appended live point is never immutable. Simplification is Douglas–Peucker with the synchronized Euclidean distance (each point against the time-interpolated position on the simplified segment, in meters on a local equirectangular projection); versions outside the caller's restriction break the track. A segment with a single point repeats it, so every segment is a valid LineString.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

get.description:
Keyframe = asOf state at `from`; each frame holds upserts and removals (tombstone, expiry, leaving the bbox) for its interval, built in one ordered pass on the transaction axis. More than 20,000 entities or 2,000,000 scanned rows → 400 FRAMES_TOO_LARGE (narrow bbox or kind). ndjson sends the keyframe line first (the envelope without `frames`), then one line per frame. Frame ends are t_i = min(from + i·step, to); (to − from)/step frames must not exceed maxFrames. With a bbox only entities with a version inside it in the range are read; the caller's restriction and `place` judge each version, and an entity whose newest version leaves them is a `left` removal.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

`date_bin` histogram over record versions (HEARTBEAT and KEYFRAME excluded unless `includeKeyframes`), optionally grouped and with alert counts. ≤ 1,000 buckets (400 TIMELINE_TOO_LARGE); 10 s timeout (503 QUERY_TIMEOUT). A range whose raw read the hourly activity rollup estimates above 1,000,000 record versions (200,000 with `timeField=ingested`, which counts far slower), from the later of `from` and `retainedFrom` for the involved sources and kinds, is refused up front with 422 TIMELINE_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED instead of running into the timeout; narrow the range, the sources or the kinds, or use getStatsTimeseries, which serves long ranges from the rollups. `bucket=auto` picks the smallest of 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 2d, 7d, 14d, 30d giving at most 200 buckets; buckets start at `from` and every bucket in range is returned, empty ones included. Without `source` or `kind`, every source the caller may see is counted. `timeField=ingested` is translated to seq bounds through seq_clock. `retainedFrom` is the latest of now − window over the involved sources. Not the same as /v1/products/timeline (051).

get.description:
Mapbox Vector Tile (layer `wind`, extent 4096) of wind points for the u/v products (`gfs`, `hrrr`): the frame sampled bilinearly on a 32 px lattice inside the 256 px tile (8×8 points at pixel centers, so the on-screen density is the same at every zoom), each with `speedMs` (m/s, 0.1), `fromDeg` (the direction the wind blows from, `(270 − atan2(v,u)·180/π) mod 360`, integer) and `barbKt` (knots rounded to a 5-kt bucket). HRRR's grid-relative winds are rotated to earth-relative at ingest. Built by PostGIS `ST_AsMVT`; an empty tile is an empty body. Cached and render-queued like raster tiles, with the same cache rule; zooms above the native max zoom are 400 TILE_OUT_OF_RANGE (clients overzoom).

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

get.description:
Ticks marked `observed|forecast`: the union of the products' frame valid times in the window, with the frame chosen per product per tick (at or before the tick with the smallest gap, honoring `maxGap`; a product with none is absent at that tick), the single run used per forecast product (its newest complete run, never mixed; `runs`), `nowIndex` (the tick nearest now) and expanded, content-addressed tile templates. `mode=seamless` joins a `past` observed product (ticks up to now) to a `future` forecast product (ticks after now). External catalog entries get synthesized ticks every `timeDimension.period` up to `now − defaultLag`, with `availability: unverified` and the external template's `{time}` filled. Default window: now − 6 h to now (+ 48 h when a forecast product is named); seamless now − 3 h to now + 18 h. At most 10 products. More than 500 ticks → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

Per product: value (or u/v with derived speed and direction), units, label, frame key, valid time, local time, age, run, method, status and attribution. Non-ok statuses carry `statusText`; no-coverage reads "outside product coverage; this is not evidence of clear weather". Never triggers an upstream fetch. Time: `latest` is the newest frame (judged stale against now); `now`, an ISO time and a past offset choose the observation frame valid at or before the time; a future offset (and any time on a forecast product) uses the newest complete forecast run, taking the step valid at or before the time. Status order: unavailable (product disabled, source failing, no frame, frame expired), no-coverage, no-data, stale, ok; a non-ok value has `value: null`.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

post.description:
A single image (`file`, PNG, JPEG or TIFF, ≤ 25 MB) plus `meta`. The running station passes it through ImageGuard before decoding, stores it with 256/1024 px thumbnails and attaches it to the matching pass: `meta.passId` when the station knows that pass, else the 049 join rule (same satellite, timestamp inside [first lock − 5 min, LOS + 5 min]), else a pass minted from the image; the pass gets a new `decoded` version. Only sources whose descriptor accepts remote media (the `satdump-{station}` family) answer; any other source, or a station whose stream is not running, is 404. `media` is a reserved segment that never routes to an IngestFormat. Each push costs one unit of the source's budget (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` when spent). Syncing SatDump's output into the inbox (rsync or Syncthing) remains the recommended remote path.

**Scope:** `open` (the source's ingest key, or an admin token, is checked by the endpoint). A `satdump-{station}` source has no minted ingest key: the operator stores the key a remote station presents as the source's `ingestKey` credential (`PUT /v1/sources/{id}/credentials`).

Names are single safe path segments (no separators, no `..`, no leading dot); every listed file needs a part and every part must be listed; images pass the ImageGuard header check (400). `dataset.json` is placed in the pass folder and every other file in the product directory: `product` when given, else the single product `dataset.json` lists, else the pass folder itself. The bundle is written atomically to `${FORESIGNAL_DATA_DIR}/rasters/satdump/{station}/incoming/{uploadId}/` (the inbox mount is read-only); the station's inbox loop processes it like a ready pass folder on its next scan (composites, thumbnails, provenance, polar GeoTIFF overlays, footprint or approximate swath) and the copy expires after 2 days. Only `satdump-{station}` sources answer; others are 404. `rasters` is a reserved segment that never routes to an IngestFormat. Each push costs one unit of the source's budget.

**Scope:** `open` (the source's ingest key, or an admin token, is checked by the endpoint). The ingest key of a `satdump-{station}` source is its `ingestKey` credential.

get.description:
Basemap-free server-rendered PNG: Natural Earth land, water and boundaries, product frames, alert geometry, place marker and range rings, scale bar, frame valid times (UTC plus the place's local time), legend, attribution and an "Automated — not an official warning" footer. The box is `bbox`, else `center` with `radiusKm` (default 50 km), else the alert's record geometry, else the place; it is snapped outwards to 0.01° once and widened to the map area's aspect, and `Foresignal-Image-Bounds` gives the result. Missing or stale frames are drawn as a labeled note ("… unavailable — not evidence of clear weather"), never omitted; a concrete ISO time at which an enabled product has no frame is 404 UNKNOWN_FRAME. Nothing fetches third-party tiles (an operator's LAN tile server, `FORESIGNAL_MAPS_BASEMAP_URL_TEMPLATE`, may replace the Natural Earth fills). Immutable only when every frame is pinned: a concrete ISO `time`, complete current frames, a pinned run for forecasts, a versioned style for every product and no `place`; otherwise a short max-age with an ETag checked before rendering. Rendered on the render pool within 2 s, else 503 RENDER_BUSY.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

get.description:
RFC 4287 Atom feed of alerts with GeoRSS-Simple geometry (`georss:point`, or `georss:polygon` for single polygons ≤ 500 vertices, else the centroid). Entries are ordered newest first by last lifecycle change. Entry `id` is `tag:foresignal,2026:{installId}/alert/{id}`, title is `shortTitle` (else the title), the alternate link is the client deep link (else `publicBaseUrl/v1/alerts/{id}`), categories carry severity and rule tags. Content is markdown rendered with commonmark-java and sanitised by an allowlist (`p, br, strong, em, code, pre, ul, ol, li, blockquote, h3–h6, a[href]` http/https only). Private-source alerts are excluded unless the token or feed key passes the private gate and `EgressPolicy.allows(FEED)`. Conditional GET: ETag over (max lifecycle timestamp, max id, filters) plus `Last-Modified`. Feed readers without headers use a 035 feed key (`/v1/k/{key}/alerts/feed.atom`). RSS 2.0 and WebSub publishing are not offered.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

**v2.0 (per-user, R2-008):** an alert carries its rule's owner from when it fired. A signed-in user sees, and acts on, the alerts of their own rules and of shared rules; another user's alert is left out of lists, feeds and streams and is 404 by id. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see all alerts; anonymous callers and feed keys see the shared ones.

post.summary: Preview a RecordMapping over a sample
post.description:
Compiles the mapping with `MappingCompiler` and applies it to the sample through the standard 008 normaliser, returning exactly what ingest would write. Writes nothing. Warnings cover unmapped input keys, fields missing from the source's `fieldSpecs`, a policy-required significant field that is missing, and a time-base mismatch with the source's `observedAtMode`. Compile errors return 400 `MAPPING_INVALID` with `errors[].field` paths such as `mapping.fields[3].unit.from`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

post.description:
Asks the chat provider (purpose `mapping-suggest`, 026 budget) for a draft mapping. The sample is untrusted data inside delimiters; the output is validated with `MappingCompiler` with up to 2 repair rounds, then previewed over the sample. The draft is never stored or applied: saving it is a separate `PUT /v1/custom-sources/{id}`. A remote provider requires `confirmEgress: true` (409 `EGRESS_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`); samples from a private source are refused for remote providers (403); no provider → 409 `LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Rebuilds state at seq S (default the current watermarkSeq, or `asOf` translated with S(T)) from record_version per tier, writing GeoParquet plus a signed manifest. Below a source's floorSeq rows come from held copies, else `400 SNAPSHOT_BEYOND_RETENTION`. Validity is judged at the transaction time of S (its ingested_at, or the requested asOf); a source whose state at S lies before its retention horizon is read from the copies of holds covering it. Private sources need `includePrivate=true`; FORBIDDEN and LOCAL_ONLY sources need `personalUse=true`, as for exports. Snapshots are export jobs of kind SNAPSHOT (list, poll and download through `/v1/exports`) and never expire unless `expiresAt` is set.

post.description:
A snapshot whose absent share is above `maxAbsentRatio` is held and the source turns degraded (docs/External-Data-Protocol.md §3.2). This releases it once: the absence tombstones are computed against the scope's current entities now and ingested; the hold and the degraded status clear.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description:
Verifies the email + Argon2id password (and the MFA code when enrolled) and issues a session bearer (166). The session carries the user's effective permissions (the union of the user's roles). A suspended or disabled account is refused (403). Repeated failures from one address are rate-limited (429). When MFA is enrolled but no `mfaCode` is given, the response reports `mfaRequired` and issues no usable session (`token` empty, `expiresAt` null); a wrong `mfaCode` (TOTP or recovery code) is the same 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS (R2-024). A session of a user holding the Admin or Operator role who has not enrolled MFA may read, enroll (enrollMfa, verifyMfa), set preferences, sign out and revoke its own sessions; every other write is 403 MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED until verifyMfa activates MFA (R2-024).

**Scope:** `open`.

Revokes the session bearer used for this request; its open SSE streams are closed. Idempotent.

**Scope:** `read`.

Sends a single-use, expiring reset link to the address when it belongs to an active account. Always returns 202 whether or not the address exists, so accounts cannot be enumerated; requires SMTP to be configured to actually deliver (170).

**Scope:** `open`.

202.description: Accepted (an email is sent only if the account exists)

post.summary: Reset a password with a reset token
post.description:
Sets a new password from the single-use token emailed by requestPasswordReset, then revokes all of the user's existing sessions. The token is consumed on success.

**Scope:** `open`.

Sets the first password for an invited user from the emailed activation token, moving the account from `invited` to `active`. The token is single-use.

**Scope:** `open`.

get.description:
Lists the calling user's own active sessions, the current one marked. For revoking another user's sessions an admin uses the user-management API (D2).

delete.description:

**Scope:** `read`.

Revokes a single session by id. Revoking the current session logs the caller out.

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:

post.description:

Null lifts the restriction; absent leaves it. The change applies to the user's next request. Requires `users.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

delete.description:
Deletes a user. By default the user's owned config (triggers, channels, personal LLM providers, saved views) is reassigned to an admin rather than deleted; pass `reassign=false` to delete it instead (168). The last remaining admin cannot be deleted (409).

**Scope:** `admin`.

parameters.name: reassign

**Scope:** `admin`.

Moves the user to `suspended`, revoking all their sessions; their account and config are kept. Requires `users.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Returns a suspended user to `active`. Requires `users.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

post.description:
