get.description:
Returns the caller's own source view over the shared collection: one entry per source the caller may see, with `enabled` and the caller's display overrides. A view is opt-out: a source the caller never turned off is `enabled` with no overrides. The instance-wide collection set is getCollectionSources. A view belongs to a signed-in user, so an API token gets `401`. Requires `self.sources`.

**Scope:** `read`.

put.description:
Replaces the caller's source view; a source left out returns to the default (enabled, no overrides). A source may be listed whether or not the instance collects it; the preference takes effect while it is in the collection set. The collector pulls a source once while any active user's view keeps it, so a view never adds a second pull. Afterwards the caller's reads (records, changes, tiles, search, statistics) show only the sources in their view. An API token gets `401`. Requires `self.sources`.

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
Returns the instance collection set: every registered source with `inCollection` (whether the instance may collect it) and `enabledByUsers` (how many active users' views keep it). The collector pulls a source once when it is in this set and some active user's view keeps it, or, while no user is active, whenever it is in this set. Requires `collection.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Sets `inCollection` for every listed source, all or nothing; a source left out keeps its state and `enabledByUsers` is ignored. Each change applies the checks of updateSource, so collecting a source without its required credentials is `409 CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED`. A source taken out of the set is pulled for no one, regardless of per-user views. Requires `collection.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

409.description: A listed source needs credentials that are not stored (CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED)

get.summary: Get my LLM budget and spend
get.description:
Returns the calling user's LLM spend this UTC month on every provider they can use: the enabled shared providers and their own personal ones, by id. `spentUsd` counts only calls made for this user (their own requests, and work done on their behalf such as enriching their alerts); calls made with an API token are the machine's and are not counted. On a shared provider `capUsd` is its `perUserMonthlyCapUsd`, the user's share; on a personal provider it is the provider's own `monthlyCapUsd`. `remainingUsd` is the cap minus the spend, never below zero, or null when uncapped. A budget belongs to a signed-in user, so an API token gets `401`. Requires `self.llm`.

**Scope:** `read`.

Returns the calling user's preferences with the defaults filled in: an unset `timezone` reads as the server's (getServerSettings), an unset `theme` as `system`, an unset `locale` as the instance notification language (`notify.defaultLanguage`). `notifications` summarizes the caller's notification preferences (listMyNotificationPreferences): `emailEnabled` is false only when the caller has email channels and every one is off, `pushEnabled` likewise for push channels (ntfy, gotify, pushover, webpush), and `quietHours` is the window every preference shares, or null when they differ or have none. Needs a signed-in session (an API token is 401). Requires `self.preferences`.

**Scope:** `read`.

put.description:
Replaces the calling user's preferences. `timezone` (an IANA zone the server knows), `locale` (a BCP 47 tag naming an ISO 639 language) and `theme` (`system`, `light` or `dark`) are replaced; absent or null resets each to its default, and an invalid value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. `ui` is replaced whole (at most 64 KiB of JSON). The timezone is the user's own (`Principal.timezone`): the user's personal notification channels render their quiet hours in it, and the Ask assistant writes the user's local time in it; stored times stay UTC. `notifications` writes through to the caller's notification preferences rather than a second copy: `emailEnabled` and `pushEnabled` turn every email or push channel on or off, `quietHours` (`HH:MM-HH:MM`, or null to clear) sets the window on every preference; a member left out, or the whole object, leaves those preferences as they are. Needs a signed-in session (an API token is 401). Requires `self.preferences`.

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
Live host disk free space, memory and database size with an overall ok/warn/critical status (177), rated against `GET /v1/settings/thresholds`. Readings are cached for up to 30 s. A `warn` or `critical` gauge also appears in `/v1/system.warnings` as `DISK_LOW`, `DISK_CRITICAL`, `MEMORY_LOW` or `MEMORY_CRITICAL`. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Settings key `thresholds`: the warn/critical disk and memory levels, the alert channels, and the source-storm and collector-backlog bounds; the defaults when never set. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces the thresholds; a breach raises /v1/system warnings and fires alerts through the channel system. Each alert is edge-triggered: entering `warn` or `critical` publishes one `system` notification (`system.disk_low`, `system.disk_critical`, `system.memory_low`, `system.memory_critical`, `system.source_storm`, `system.collector_backlog`, `system.user_rate_limited`) and returning to normal publishes one recovery (`system.disk_recovered`, `system.memory_recovered`, `system.source_storm_cleared`, `system.collector_backlog_cleared`, `system.user_rate_limit_cleared`). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

get.description:
Dry run of the current retention policy: what the next run would prune per subsystem (records per kind, TRACK leaves, frames, media, stopped chronicles), with a size estimate and nothing deleted (B2/178). It uses the settings the next run applies, including a window the database-size cap has stepped down to; with `capHistory` off it shows today's per-subsystem windows. Frames pinned by a chronicle are not counted; quota eviction is not previewed. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Lists cold-storage archive segments with sizes and status, newest first (B3/179). This is the archival-tier inventory (`archive_manifest`); the compliance cold-archive catalog of legal holds is getArchiveCatalog. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-016:** an unknown `status` or a cursor this endpoint did not issue is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

post.description:
Starts an archival pass now: select data older than the cutoff, export to the target with a verified checksum, mark archived, then purge from the hot store (B3/179). Returns the created segment. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-016:** the pass plans a retention run with the archived sources' STANDARD windows capped to now − cutoff (no other source's window moves), writes exactly the rows that plan removes (and the rows of TRACK partitions about to be dropped) as one gzip NDJSON file per source, offloads each to the tier and verifies it there (SHA-256 read back on the external disk; ETag and size on S3/Glacier), records the manifest (`complete`), and only then runs the planned retention pass, so the purge goes through the existing delete, drop and head-purge paths. A failed export or verification purges nothing, marks the segment `failed` and raises the operational alert `system.archive_failed`. The pass holds the retention job's single-run guard: while retention or another archive pass runs, the answer is 409 ALREADY_RUNNING. 409 ARCHIVE_NOT_CONFIGURED when the archive is off, or an s3/glacier target lacks its settings or secrets.

Pulls an archive segment back from cold storage into the hot store (B3/179). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-016:** `confirm: true` is required (400 otherwise). Each file is pulled from its tier and its SHA-256 checked, then its rows are loaded into the restore area `record_version_restored` (keyed by the archive id), not back into record_version, whose partitions for those seqs are gone and whose retention would delete them again. A Glacier segment stays `restoring` while S3 thaws its objects (typically hours); the runner asks again each minute. A restore may be large and slow. 409 ALREADY_RESTORED, ALREADY_RUNNING (the segment or another restore is in progress), ARCHIVE_NOT_RESTORABLE (a failed segment) or ARCHIVE_NOT_CONFIGURED (s3/glacier settings missing).

get.description:
Settings key `backup`; secrets are never returned (only `secretsSet`). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces backup settings; an omitted secret keeps the stored one. Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** every problem is one 400: `enabled` and `target` are required, `schedule` must be a six-field cron expression, `external` needs an absolute `root`, `s3` needs `s3.endpoint` and `s3.bucket`, `keepBackups` is 1 to 10000 or null. The S3 endpoint must pass the outbound URL policy (400 URL_NOT_ALLOWED). Secrets are stored encrypted and never returned.

get.description:
Lists backup artifacts with type, size and status (180). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** newest first; `type` filters to one type.

post.description:
Starts a DB (pg_dump/base) or config-export backup to the configured target (B4/180). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** returns the `pending` backup; a worker then runs `pg_dump --format=custom` of the application database (the password goes to it as `PGPASSWORD`, never on its command line) and/or writes the `exportSettings` bundle, stores each file on the target through the R2-016 archive tiers and verifies it there, marks the backup `complete`, and prunes complete backups of that type beyond `keepBackups`. A failure marks it `failed` with `error` and raises the operational alert `system.backup_failed`; when `pg_dump` is not on the server's PATH, a database backup fails with that reason and the server carries on. 409 BACKUP_NOT_CONFIGURED while backups are off, or an `s3` target lacks its bucket or secrets, or an `external` target its root; 409 ALREADY_RUNNING while another backup or restore runs.

Restores the instance from a backup; destructive, so `confirm` must be true (180). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** a `config` backup is imported at once through `importSettings` (atomic: a 400 listing every error applies nothing); the answer is the `restored` backup with its `importReport`. A `database` or `full` backup is restored in the background (the answer is the `restoring` backup) with `pg_restore --clean --if-exists --single-transaction` into the live database: it replaces every table, the backup history included, then brings the schema forward with the server's migrations and marks the backup `restored`. **Operational caveat:** the restore takes locks on every table, so ingest and API writes wait on it, and anything written after the backup was taken is lost; pause collection first and restart the server afterwards so every cache is rebuilt. While it runs, no retention or archive pass starts. A failed restore puts the backup's previous status back with `error` and raises `system.backup_failed`. 409 ALREADY_RUNNING while a backup, restore, retention or archive pass runs; 409 BACKUP_NOT_RESTORABLE for a failed backup, or a config bundle whose stored copy is missing or does not match its checksum (the reason is kept in `error`); 409 BACKUP_NOT_CONFIGURED for an `s3` backup when the settings have no bucket or secrets.

400.description: `confirm` is not true, or the request or the stored config bundle is invalid (VALIDATION_FAILED)

get.description:
Lists the egress pool with per-route health and last observed exit IP (C1/181). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** ordered by name; 400 for a cursor this server did not issue.

post.description:
Adds a proxy, WireGuard profile or bound interface to the egress pool; credentials are stored encrypted, never returned. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** `url` is `http://host:port` or `socks5://host:port` (no path, no credentials in it) for those types, and its host must pass the outbound URL policy's `LAN_ALLOWED` profile (400 URL_NOT_ALLOWED otherwise); `interface` takes `boundInterface` (an interface name or an address literal); names are unique ignoring case; `wireguard` takes `secrets.wireguardConfig` and is recorded but always unavailable, because the server cannot bring a tunnel up. Secrets are sealed with the instance key and never returned; `secretsSet` names those stored.

get.description:
Returns one egress route by id. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces an egress route; an omitted secret keeps the stored one. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** the same validation as create; an omitted `secrets` member keeps the stored value, an empty string or null clears it, and a secret the new type cannot use is dropped.

delete.description:
Removes an egress route. Sources pinned to it fall back to the default route. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** sources pinned to the route lose the pin, and the default route is cleared when it was this one.

post.description:
Makes a probe call through the route and reports the observed public exit IP and latency; nothing is persisted beyond the route's health (C1/181). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** one `GET` of the configured exit-IP service (`foresignal.egress.probe-url`, default `https://checkip.amazonaws.com/`, checked against the public-only outbound policy) through the route. Always 200: `ok` false with a `message` when the route is unavailable or the call fails. A passing test records `exitIp` on the route.

get.description:
Returns reachability, latency, exit IP and backoff state for one route. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** health is held in memory and starts empty at restart; three consecutive failures mark the route unreachable, skip it in rotation and raise `system.egress_unhealthy`; a later success raises `system.egress_recovered`. `sources` lists the per-source holds on the route.

Settings key `egress`; the rotation policy and default route. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces the rotation policy and default route. Default is direct (no egress routing). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** 400 for an unknown `rotation`, or a `defaultRoute` that names no route. With rotation on and no usable route for a source, its pull fails rather than going direct.

Pins a source to an egress route, or excludes it from rotation (e.g. a geo-locked source to an in-region exit). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-018:** 404 UNKNOWN_SOURCE for a source this server does not have; 400 for a `routeId` that names no route.

get.description:
Lists the first-party aggregators across RF/sensor domains with status and the public sources each supersedes (C3). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** every domain is listed. adsb is implemented, ais since R2-020, datalink since R2-021, satellite since R2-022 and ground-sensors since R2-023, so every domain reads `implemented: true`; a domain whose backend a server does not have reads `implemented: false` and `status: unconfigured`.

Returns the aggregator for one domain (adsb, ais, datalink, satellite, ground-sensors). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** 404 UNKNOWN_AGGREGATOR for any other domain.

put.description:
Enables and configures a domain's first-party aggregator and, by default, defaults the superseded public/mirror sources off (they stay in the catalog as opt-in fallbacks). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** the configuration is replaced whole. adsb writes `endpoint` (and `config.band`) to the `local-adsb-aggregator` source and turns it on while the aggregator is live (enabled with an endpoint), off otherwise. While live with `disableSupersededSources`, every registered `adsblol-*`, `adsbfi-*` and `airplaneslive-*` source and `gpsjam-daily` that is on is turned off, and seeding and `enable-core`/`enable-free` leave them off; when the aggregator stops being live, or `disableSupersededSources` is false, the sources it turned off are turned back on. 400 for a bad member, an endpoint that is not an http(s) aircraft.json URL (adsb) or a tcp:// or udp:// NMEA endpoint (ais, R2-020; udp:// needs config.allowSenders) or a tcp://host decoder host with at least one decoder selected (datalink, R2-021) or an http(s) SatDump URL without config.location (satellite, R2-022) or any endpoint, an unknown sensor or member, or no sensor enabled (ground-sensors, R2-023, where a source's own parameter error is reported at the sensor's member) or does not resolve to a local address, or `enabled: true` on a domain this server has no backend for. A live aggregator whose source starts failing raises `system.aggregator_down` (and `system.aggregator_recovered` when it is healthy again).

**R2-023:** ground-sensors is live while enabled with a sensor enabled. Each enabled sensor's members are written into its local read, which is turned on while live; a read a previous configuration drove and this one does not is turned off, and one never driven is left alone. Only the enabled sensors' mirrors are superseded, and a configuration that supersedes less turns the rest back on.

post.description:
Probes the aggregator's local endpoint and reports reachability and a sample object count; nothing is persisted. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** reads the stored endpoint once through the aggregator's source (its budget and pinning apply). Always 200; `ok` false with a `message` when nothing is configured, the endpoint cannot be reached, or the answer is not readsb aircraft.json. `sampleCount` is the number of aircraft in it.

**R2-020:** for ais, listens to the stored NMEA endpoint for 10 s through `local-ais-aggregator` and reports the vessel records decoded (at most 100); a live UDP listener, which cannot be bound twice, is reported from its statistics (distinct MMSIs in the last 10 minutes).

**R2-021:** for datalink, listens to every selected read (ACARS/VDLM2/HFDL and APRS) at once for 10 s and sums the messages decoded; `reachable` is false only when no selected read could be connected.

**R2-022:** for satellite, runs the satdump-aggregator station for 10 s (its /api read and inbox scan) and counts the records it produced: station state, passes and products.

**R2-023:** for ground-sensors, probes every enabled sensor's polling or streaming read at once for 10 s and sums the records; a push source (seismic, same, the MeshCore bridge) or a live local-sonde UDP listener is reachable once it has received data. A failing sensor is named in `message`; `reachable` is false only when every sensor fails.

Starts TOTP enrollment and returns the secret and provisioning URI; enrollment is not active until verifyMfa confirms a code. Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

Confirms a pending TOTP enrollment with a current code, enabling MFA for the account; that answer carries the first recovery codes once (`recoveryCodes`). Once MFA is active it is the step-up check: a current TOTP or unused recovery code. A code is within one 30 s step of now and never accepted twice. 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID for a wrong, expired or reused code; at most 10 code checks a minute per user (429). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

Disables MFA after re-authenticating with a code or the account password. A role that requires MFA (Admin, Operator) refuses this (409 MFA_REQUIRED; an administrator reset is the way out); 409 MFA_NOT_ENABLED with nothing to disable. A wrong code is 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID, a wrong password 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; at most 10 code checks a minute per user (429). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
Generates a fresh set of single-use recovery codes, invalidating any previous set; shown once. Each is accepted once wherever a TOTP code is (login, verifyMfa, disableMfa). Requires MFA to be enabled (409 MFA_NOT_ENABLED). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

Lists the API tokens owned by the calling user (user-attributable machine tokens, D2/188). An admin manages all tokens via /v1/tokens. Any signed-in user; needs a session (an API token is 401). Revoked tokens are listed with `revokedAt`; a value is never returned (R2-025).

**Scope:** `read`.

post.description:
Mints an API token owned by the calling user, with the existing area/path/tile-key restrictions; its scope cannot exceed the caller's own permissions (D2/188). The secret is shown once. Any signed-in user; needs a session (an API token is 401), so a token never mints another (R2-025). The token is `createdVia: self` and owned by the caller's principal; `principalId` is refused (400). Its scope is at most `admin` for a user holding every permission, `agent` for one whose sessions are `agent` or `admin`, else `read`; `privateAccess` needs an admin-derived session; anything wider is 403 TOKEN_EXCEEDS_USER. On every request the token is capped again by its owner's current roles, narrowed by the owner's data restriction, refused (401) while the owner may not sign in, and audited as the owner (R2-025).

**Scope:** `read`.

403.description: Caller lacks the required permission, or the token would reach further than the caller (TOKEN_EXCEEDS_USER, R2-025)

delete.summary: Revoke one of my API tokens
delete.description:
Revokes an API token owned by the calling user. Any signed-in user; needs a session (an API token is 401). A token the caller does not own is 404, as if it did not exist; the revoked token stops authenticating at once (R2-025).

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
Returns a user's own quota (D5/189, R2-026): the limits set for that user, null where the instance default applies. The effective quota is what `getMyQuota` reports to the user. Requires `users.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces a user's own quota whole (R2-026): every member is a non-negative integer or null, and null (or absent) uses the instance default; an unknown member is 400. A quota with every member null removes the user's own limits. `0` allows nothing: no API requests, or no further alert rules, channels, views or stored bytes. `apiRateLimitPerMinute` limits the user's sessions and own API tokens together (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After, `class: user`); when a user is refused in every minute for 5 minutes an operational alert `system.user_rate_limited` is raised, and `system.user_rate_limit_cleared` once a minute passes without a refusal. The count and storage limits apply when the user creates (409 QUOTA_EXCEEDED). Requires `users.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

get.description:
Returns the calling user's effective quota (their own limits over the instance default; null is unlimited) and current usage: `alerts`, `channels` and `savedViews` (the trigger rules, notification channels and saved views they own), `storageBytes` (their uploaded attachments plus the JSON of the workspaces they own) and `apiRequestsThisMinute` (requests in the current clock minute across their sessions and own API tokens) (D5/189, R2-026). A session or a user's own API token (R2-025); an API token with no user has no quota and gets 401.

**Scope:** `read`.

Reports whether the instance still needs first-run setup: `firstRun` while no user exists (C4/190, R2-027). Open, so the admin app can start the setup wizard before any account exists. `smtpConfigured` is true when account email is enabled with a host; `sourcesEnabled` counts the sources in the collection set; `apiVersion` is `info.version`.

**Scope:** `open`.

post.description:
Bootstraps a fresh instance (C4/190, R2-027). Only the bootstrap admin token printed at first start may call it (403 for any other token or a session) and only while no user exists (409 ALREADY_SETUP after). It creates the first admin, active at once with the built-in Admin role and the given password (checked against the password policy); moves what the v1 operator owned through the instance `owner` principal (their personal channels and workspaces, and any rule, view or LLM provider bound to it) to that admin, leaving every owner-less row (source, collector and server settings, global channels, shared LLM providers, existing rules and views) shared; optionally seeds SMTP (as `updateSmtpSettings`), enables `sources` in the collection set, and stores `thresholds` and `retention` (as their settings operations); and signs the admin in. All of it is one transaction: a body refused anywhere changes nothing. The session is gated to MFA enrollment until the admin enrolls (R2-024). API tokens are not touched.

**Scope:** `admin`.

400.description: Invalid request body (VALIDATION_FAILED, PASSWORD_POLICY): a bad admin email, name or password, an unknown member or source id, or SMTP, threshold or retention settings the settings operations refuse

409.description: Already set up: a user exists (ALREADY_SETUP); or a source in `sources` needs credentials first (CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED)

403.description: The caller is not the bootstrap admin token (FORBIDDEN)

get.description:
Target languages, translated fields, engine, budget cap and source-language confidence for translating foreign-language news at ingest (NP-002), with the current translation spend.

**Scope:** `admin`.

put.description:
Replaces the settings. Takes effect for news ingested afterwards; an already-translated article is not translated again unless its source text changes.

**Scope:** `admin`.

get.description:
The outlets and languages the caller follows, which scope the caller's editions (NP-003). A caller who never set any has none, which is no restriction. Subscriptions belong to a signed-in user, so an API token gets `401`. Requires `self.sources`.

**Scope:** `read`.

put.description:
Replaces the caller's news subscriptions; an empty list removes every restriction. An unknown outlet id or a malformed language tag is a 400. An API token gets `401`. Requires `self.sources`.

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
The caller's editions: the briefings the calling user owns (`Briefing.ownerUserId`, NP-003), newest first. An edition is created, changed, run and deleted through the briefing operations. Any signed-in user; an API token gets `401`.

**Scope:** `read`.

post.description:
Creates an edition the calling user owns, without needing agent scope (2.1.1). The body is a `BriefingInput`; `ownerUserId` is ignored and forced to the caller. The edition is then listed by `listMyEditions` and managed through the other `/v1/me/editions` operations. Any signed-in user holding `self.editions`; an API token is 401.

**Scope:** `read`.

put.description:
Updates an edition the calling user owns (2.1.1). The body is a `BriefingInput`; `ownerUserId` is forced to the caller. 404 unless the edition exists and the caller owns it. Any signed-in user holding `self.editions`.

**Scope:** `read`.

delete.description:
Deletes an edition the calling user owns (2.1.1). 404 unless the edition exists and the caller owns it. Any signed-in user holding `self.editions`.

**Scope:** `read`.

post.description:
Runs an edition the calling user owns on demand (2.1.1), producing a run delivered to the edition's targets. 404 unless the edition exists and the caller owns it. Any signed-in user holding `self.editions`.

**Scope:** `read`.

get.description:
The edition's latest successful run as a complete, standalone HTML page (NP-005): a stable, always-current newspaper site. `Accept: application/json` or `?format=json` returns the `EditionSite` (canonical, feed-key and share URLs) instead. Feed keys work through `/v1/k/{key}/editions/{briefingId}/site`, with asset URLs carrying the same key; a share link to the site grants it and its assets only, read-only and revocable. Same visibility as the podcast feed: 404 unless the edition is visible to the caller (its owner, its feed key or its share link for an owned edition), runs citing private sources only behind the private gate, and 404 while the site is off or before the first successful run. Strong ETag and `Last-Modified`; 304 on a match.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

monthlyCapUsd.description: Money cap per UTC calendar month for a paid source (135; X default 25, the descriptor's `defaultBudget`). Set with `updateSource`; the budget object is replaced whole, so leaving it out (or null) returns the source to its default cap (none for free sources). Once the month's spend (`SourceHealth.spentUsdThisMonth`) reaches it, the budget governor refuses every request of the source until the next month begins (a push or upload is refused 429 BUDGET_EXCEEDED) and the source's health is `degraded` with the reason. X's platform cap (`social.x.monthlyCapUsd`, default 25) applies as well.

allowed.description: When non-empty, the only accepted values. For type lan-url it lists the accepted URL schemes instead (069): empty means http, https, ws and wss; tcp (tcp://host:port, resolved once to a loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local address and pinned) and udp (udp://bindHost:port, bindHost 0.0.0.0, :: or a local interface address, with the required string-list companion allowSenders of private IPs or CIDRs) are accepted only when listed; so are mqtt and mqtts (083: an operator's broker, mqtt://host:port or mqtts://host:port, pinned to a private address like tcp). The port of a tcp, udp, mqtt or mqtts URL is always explicit.

mode.description: Collection mode; `derived` sources are fed by ChangeBus or frame events and never polled

minInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h); null for a source that is not polled (streaming or push)

defaultInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h); null for a source that is not polled (streaming or push)

observedAtMode.description: Fixed time base: upstream timestamps, or receipt time for every record (TIME_IMPUTED)

ttlAnchor.description: Axis for TTL and keyframes (TRACK must be OBSERVED; STANDARD defaults to RECEIVED)

defaultIngestPolicy.description: The descriptor's policy with the Core-Data-Model §5.1 defaults filled in (ALL keyframe = ttl − pollInterval − 30s or `none`; edgeMinInterval = minInterval / 2)

volatileFields.description: Top-level payload keys left out of hashes and kinematic state

significantFields.description: Keys whose change persists SIGNIFICANT; empty = every non-volatile key

defaultRetention.description: STANDARD only. ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h)

skewTolerance.description: Future-clamp tolerance before FUTURE_CLAMPED is flagged. ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h)

allowNullIsland.description: Keep exact (0,0) points instead of nulling them

products.description: Raster product ids served by this source

titleField.description: Payload key used as record title

entityKeys.description: Entity key type → top-level payload field (icao24, registration, mmsi, imo, callsign …)

fieldSpecs.description: Declared payload fields keyed by top-level name

aggBelowZoom.description: Tiles aggregate below this zoom with agg=auto; null = never

startField.description: Payload key of an interval start (with endField)

endField.description: Payload key of an interval end (with startField)

private.description: Personal data: excluded from anonymous reads, tiles and other egress paths

privatePrecisionDecimals.description: Coordinate decimals kept for private sources

egress.description: LOCAL_ONLY: served to this instance's own API clients (reads, tiles, SSE, MCP, an export to the caller) and notifications, never re-served by sinks (110), federation (113), share links (112) or feeds and feed keys; off-box archive exports (111) refuse it too. Set by the upstream's terms: opensky-states is LOCAL_ONLY (062), the ODbL adsb.lol sources are OPEN. MLAT positions are never redistributable regardless (069).

egressOverridable.description: The operator may override `egress` in SourceSettings (local receivers, 069)

llmNotice.description: Notice appended whenever this source's records are placed in an LLM context (090; e.g. OpenFEMA eligibility notice)

licenceTerms.description: Structured terms; derived from the catalogue when only `licence` is set and matches an id

reliability.description: Default reliability (F unless set); overridable per source

derivedFrom.description: DERIVED sources: input source ids; the most restrictive input terms apply

upstreamRefFields.description: Payload fields carrying the upstream's own event id ('field', or 'field@namespace' so differently named fields of two sources compare; '$externalId' is the record's external id) or, prefixed 'cite:', the cited original source (a URL, domain or name). Empty means the default from intel/originators.json; GET /v1/sources shows the fields in force.

embed.description: Embed this source's records for semantic search (default true when the source declares embedFields)

credentialsSet.description: True if credentials are stored (values never returned)

effectiveIngestPolicy.description: Override if set, else the descriptor default

effectiveRetention.description: Effective retention window (TRACK: `retention.trackWindow`). ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h)

statsIncludePrivate.description: Roll up this private source anyway (038 `stats.includePrivate[sourceId]`)

private.description: Operator tightening to private (039); a descriptor-private source cannot be made public

regionTagging.description: Default eager for STANDARD, lazy for TRACK (040)

downsampleInterval.description: Per-source downsample interval override (TRACK sources only). ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h)

egress.description: Operator override of the descriptor egress; only when `egressOverridable` (else 400 EGRESS_FIXED); null = descriptor default

reliability.description: Operator override of the descriptor reliability; null = descriptor default

embed.description: Embed this source's records for semantic search (027). `true` is refused (400 VALIDATION_FAILED, field `embed`) when the source declares no embedFields or is private; turning it off deletes the source's record documents.

ingestPolicy.description: Explicit null clears the override; omitted leaves it unchanged. Invalid → 400 INGEST_POLICY_INVALID

downsampleInterval.description: TRACK sources only (STANDARD → 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, field `downsampleInterval`); explicit null clears it. ISO-8601 duration (P7D, PT15M) or shorthand (7d, 15m, 12h)

egress.description: Egress override; accepted only when the descriptor is `egressOverridable` (400 EGRESS_FIXED otherwise); null reverts to the descriptor

reliability.description: Admiralty reliability override; null reverts to the descriptor default

SourceSettingsUpdate.description: Partial update; omitted fields unchanged. retention=null reverts to the default (400 RETENTION_TIER_FIXED on TRACK sources); ingestPolicy=null clears the policy override.

mode.description: Collection mode; `derived` sources are fed by ChangeBus or frame events and never polled

credentialsRequired.description: True if any credential field is required

lastDataAt.description: Last fetch or flush that returned records (never a 304)
Last OK fetch or stream flush with records (a 304 never sets it)

budgetHoursRemaining.description: Hours until today's budget is exhausted at the last hour's rate; null when that rate is 0

newestFrameAt.description: Product sources: newest frame time (frame-age health rule)

frameAgeSeconds.description: Product sources: age of the newest frame

details.description: Adapter-specific health details; omitted when there are none. aisstream (063): `compressionEnabled` (from its SubscriptionConfirmation), `perMessageDeflate` (whether the handshake negotiated it; present while connected) and `vessels` (vessels held in the merged state)

spentUsdThisMonth.description: Paid adapters: money spent this UTC calendar month (135), against `budget.monthlyCapUsd`

ingestedAt.description: Versions, history and asOf responses only

attribution.description: null when the source has no attribution line

title.description: record_head.title (titleField, else title > name > callsign > place > r > hex > mmsi)

persistedObservedAt.description: observedAt of the persisted version (observedAt may be newer from live updates)

eventTime.description: Discrete event time or measurement period start

validFrom.description: Start of validity (`onset ?? effective` for alerts, scheduled start for road events); nullable, hashed like validUntil

live.description: True when live state differs from the persisted version (record_live.dirty)

qaFlags.description: Quality bitmask: 1 FUTURE_CLAMPED, 2 GEOMETRY_FIXED, 4 NULL_ISLAND, 8 TIME_IMPUTED, 16 POSITION_STALE

observer.description: Only with include=observer for agent/admin tokens or when security.exposeObserver is on; otherwise omitted

entityId.description: Canonical entity from the record's open link; present with `include=entity`

aircraft.note: Altitudes in meters (datum labels in fieldSpecs); 978 MHz local receivers add `band` (`978`). Shared readsb mapper (062), reused by 069 and 080. posSource adsb|adsr|adsc|mlat|tisb|modes|other (readsb, local receivers; `other` for local-sbs), adsb|asterix|mlat|flarm (OpenSky). local-adsb and local-sbs records carry one observer (the receiver itself, with rssi in dBFS for local-adsb). MLAT positions are never redistributable (069).

vessel.note: Identical keys across vessel sources (085 follows 063, through the shared VesselStateMerger and VesselDescriptors); 059's `aiscatcher` preset maps AIS-catcher JSON to the same kind. 085: quality.accuracyMeters 10 (position accuracy flag high), 100 (low) or 185 (type 27); quality.extra ais.rot (raw ROT_AIS) and ais.pos_acc; ais-kystverket and local-ais-{n} name the receiving station as observer; class is absent for ais-digitraffic (not reported).

satellite.note: OMM keys verbatim; no geometry (clients propagate with SGP4); externalId = NORAD_CAT_ID.

conjunction.note: externalId `{lowNorad}-{highNorad}-{TCA epoch minute}`; eventTime = TCA; no geometry.

launch.note: eventTime = net, observedAt = last_updated; geometry = pad point.

reentry-prediction.note: Optional source, disabled by default, LOCAL_ONLY (Space-Track User Agreement). externalId = NORAD_CAT_ID; observedAt = MSG_EPOCH; eventTime = DECAY_EPOCH; `window` in minutes. The unverified TIP fields LAT, LON, INCL, DIRECTION, REV, HIGH_INTEREST and NEXT_REPORT become lat, lon, inclination, direction, rev, highInterest and nextReport when present; geometry Point(LON, LAT) with geometryNote.

example.geometryNote: predicted position at 10 km altitude, not an impact point

satellite-pass.note: status `predicted` (064), then `receiving|recorded|decoded|failed` for SatDump station passes (049: `receiving` at AOS, `recorded` at LOS with `rf{}`, `decoded` when products join, `failed` when none arrived by LOS + 20 min although the station had lock); 064: `satellite-passes` geometry = ground track (0.01°), times rounded to 10 s, tombstoned at LOS + 10 min; a SatDump station predicts its `predictNorad` satellites as `predicted` versions under its own externalId, reused by a session or dataset whose AOS is within ±5 min, and a predicted pass with no session by LOS + 20 min becomes `missed` (station healthy) or is tombstoned. 049: externalId `{station}:{satKey}:{aosEpochMinute}`, eventTime = AOS, observedAt = the latest status time, geometry = the station point (054 upgrades it to footprints or swaths), retention 365 d; `products[]` = `{instrument, composite, mediaId, thumbMediaId}` (054 adds `productId`, `frameKey`, `tilesTemplate`); `pipelineId` and `satdumpVersion` only when the station reports them.

fire-detection.note: Shared with 048 `goes-fdc` and `hms-fire`; confidenceClass `low|nominal|high`. `nasa-firms` (065): externalId {SOURCE}:{acq_date}:{HHMM}:{lat 4dp}:{lon 4dp}, observedAt = eventTime = acq_date + acq_time (UTC), TTL 24 h from acquisition; frpMw is the FIRMS frp column (named as in goes-fdc and hms-fire); confidence is raw (l|n|h for VIIRS, 0-100 for MODIS), confidenceClass low below 30, nominal 30-79, high from 80 for MODIS; instrument VIIRS, MODIS or OLI from the product; type only for MODIS when present. `goes-fdc`: externalId g19:{col}:{row} (FDC CONUS pixel), mask 10-13 or 30-33, observedAt = scan start, eventTime = first sighting, frpMw and areaKm2 to 2 significant figures, tempK to 10 K; tombstoned after 3 processed scans without the pixel. `hms-fire`: externalId hms:{yearDay}:{hhmm}:{lat 4dp}:{lon 4dp}, observedAt = eventTime = detection time, frpMw left out when HMS reports -999, TTL 24 h. `cwfis-hotspots` (075, CWFIS GeoServer public:hotspots_last24hrs, duplicates FIRMS and is kept for its fire-behavior prediction fields (the Canadian FBP System)): externalId {rep_date}:{lat 5dp}:{lon 5dp}:{satellite}, observedAt = eventTime = rep_date, TTL 24 h from the report time; hfi kW/m, ros m/min, cfb %, sfc and tfc kg/m2, frp MW, fuel the FBP fuel type.

conflict-event.note: acled is LOCAL_ONLY (081). `gdelt-events` (066): externalId GlobalEventID; observedAt = DATEADDED (UTC), eventTime = start of the UTC Day; TTL 24 h from receipt; CAMEO root codes 13-20 by default; event codes are strings that keep their leading zeros; geoPrecision country|adm1|city, geometryApproximate true for country and adm1 centroids; actionGeoCountry is FIPS 10-4 and actionGeoCountryIso its ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 when the country table knows it; summary (the only embedded field) is "{actor1Name|Unknown actor} — {cameoRoot} — {actor2Name} in {actionGeoName}", at most 200 characters, built from codes and names only; sourceUrl is untrusted and never fetched. Machine-coded from news: a record does not confirm that the event happened.

tsunami-warning.note: Shared CAP mapper (067); cancellation is a `state: cancelled` version, never a tombstone.

gnss-fix.note: Private source (operator location). One record per gpsd device; observedAt = TPV time; altHAE only with a 3D fix; fixQuality none|2d|3d; navDegraded = mode < 3 || uSat < 4 || eph > 50 (069).

receiver-status.note: state `ok|low-rate|silent` (low-rate below the minMessagesPerSec param, default 1.0); observedAt = last1min.end of readsb stats.json; noiseDbfs and aircraftWithPos only when the receiver reports them (069).

weather-observation.note: wxstation-davis-{n} and wxstation-ecowitt-{n} (069) poll the operator's station on the LAN and emit SI units with the preset keys; indoorTempC and indoorRh only with includeIndoor; geometry is the configured lat/lon rounded to 2 decimals. Davis: observedAt = eventTime = data.ts. Ecowitt (experimental): no timestamp in the body, observedAt imputed at receipt.

transit-vehicle.note: TRACK, TTL 5 min (ttlAnchor observed), SAMPLED {15s, 240s, 150 m, thresholds, edgeMin 8s}; significant routeId, tripId, directionId, label, mode; threshold bearing 30 degrees. observedAt is fixed per feed: the vehicle timestamp (VEHICLE; untimed vehicles are dropped and counted) or the header timestamp (HEADER, and every transit-mdb-{id}). Enums by GTFS-RT proto name; bearing in degrees, speedMs in m/s; mode bus|tram|subway|rail|ferry|unknown; licensePlate is never stored. Geometry Point, quality.positionSource reported (070).

transit-alert.note: STANDARD, ALL, no TTL. observedAt = header timestamp; validFrom = eventTime = earliest impact_period start (else the deprecated active_period); validUntil = latest end only when every period has one. Texts in the translation chosen by the source's language param (default en), at most 4 KB each; periods are ISO {start, end} pairs (at most 20); informed holds up to 50 {agencyId, routeId, routeType, stopId, tripId}. No geometry. An alert missing from a later FULL_DATASET feed, or marked is_deleted, is tombstoned (070).

bikeshare-station.note: STANDARD, LATEST {keyframe 20m, edgeMinInterval 30s}, TTL 30 min (anchored on receipt); significant name, capacity, isInstalled, isRenting, isReturning, availability, so bike and dock counts are live updates. observedAt = station_status.last_reported (a station without one is dropped). availability `out-of-service|empty|low|full|ok`: out-of-service when not installed or not renting, empty at 0 bikes, low at 2 or fewer, full at 0 docks, else ok. ebikesAvailable only from GBFS 1.x/2.x feeds. system is the reviewed system id. One source per reviewed docked system; redirects refused (071).

camera.note: STANDARD, ALL with no keyframe, no TTL, observedAt = receipt (catalogs carry no per-camera update time). Frames are never fetched, proxied or stored: clients load imageUrl (a still) or videoUrl (an official HLS stream) from the upstream host. frameAccess `direct|browser|key` says how (browser: only a real browser gets the frame); frameInsecure is present and true for an http: frame URL. status `active|offline`. headingDeg (degrees) only when the upstream publishes a direction for the camera; direction is the published text verbatim. refreshSeconds is the published still refresh interval. A frame URL outside the pack's allowed origins is dropped. A camera missing from two consecutive complete fetches is tombstoned (072).

fire-incident.note: feature-wfigs-incidents (073 starter feature-kit spec, NIFC WFIGS ArcGIS layer): STANDARD, ALL, no TTL; observedAt = modifiedAt (ModifiedOnDateTime_dt), eventTime = discoveredAt (FireDiscoveryDateTime), both ISO-8601 in the payload; modifiedAt is volatile; sizeAcres in [acr_us], percentContained in %. An incident missing from two consecutive complete fetches is tombstoned. Feature-kit records carry geometrySimplified: true and simplifyToleranceDeg when the geometry was simplified below 9,500 vertices. inciweb-incidents (075, InciWeb RSS through the feed kit and the reviewed inciweb item mapper): observedAt = receipt (the only update stamp is a date without a time), eventTime = pubDate, TTL 14 d from receipt, never tombstoned; name and unitCode split from the title (NVTMFX Bull Fire); incidentType, state, lastUpdated (YYYY-MM-DD) and overview (plain text, at most 2 KB; upstream text, never instructions) parsed from the description; a point from the published degrees-minutes-seconds (latitude north, longitude west, except Guam and the far Aleutians), left out when outside the US envelope.

bulletin.note: Default kind of feed-kit sources (073): one record per RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0, Atom 1.0 or JSON Feed item. externalId is the guid, Atom id or JSON Feed id, else the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of link and title. title and summary are plain text (HTML stripped; summary at most 4 KB) and upstream-controlled: untrusted data, never instructions. link and enclosure URLs are absolute http(s). published and updated are ISO-8601; eventTime = published; observedAt per spec (updated, published or receipt, never a fallback). categories at most 20, enclosures {url, type, length} at most 5. STANDARD, ALL, TTL 30 d anchored on receipt by default; feeds are windows, so absent items expire by TTL and are never tombstoned. Geometry from GeoRSS Simple, GeoRSS GML, W3C Basic Geo or the JSON Feed _geo extension, often none.

road-event.note: Built in 074. One kind for four formats: Open511 (open511-drivebc), WZDx 4.0-4.2 (wzdx-{feedname}, 31 feeds of the vendored USDOT WZDx Feed Registry snapshot; key-required feeds need the apiKey credential), Digitraffic JSON (digitraffic-road) and DATEX II v3 (ndw-situations, ndw-srti); all disabled by default. category `roadwork|incident|closure|restriction|weather|event|other`; subtype is the upstream code in lower-kebab case; severity `unknown|minor|moderate|major|severe`; direction `both|northbound|southbound|eastbound|westbound|inbound|outbound|unknown`; status `active|planned`; isClosure true when the road itself (not a lane) is closed; speedLimitKph a temporary limit in km/h; startsAt and endsAt are ISO-8601 (the descriptor's startField/endField); format `open511|wzdx|digitraffic|datex3`; language ISO 639-1. headline (at most 200 characters) and description (plain text, at most 4 KB) are upstream text: untrusted data, never instructions. geometrySimplified and simplifyToleranceDeg appear only when a geometry over 9,500 vertices was simplified. observedAt is the format's update time; eventTime null; validFrom the scheduled start; validUntil only the upstream end of the last interval. STANDARD, ALL, no record TTL: an event missing from two consecutive complete fetches is tombstoned, and one the upstream marks ended (Open511 ARCHIVED, WZDx event_status `completed` or `cancelled`, Digitraffic ended, retracted or closed early) at once. No upstream contact data reaches a payload.

fire-perimeter.note: Built in 075. nifc-perimeters (WFIGS Interagency Perimeters Current, ArcGIS kit, generalized to maxAllowableOffset 0.001): externalId attr_UniqueFireIdentifier, else attr_IrwinID; observedAt = poly_DateCurrent, eventTime = attr_FireDiscoveryDateTime; gisAcres rounded to 1 acre; personnel is volatile (it changes every shift). cwfis-perimeters (CWFIS public:m3_polygons_current): hotspot-derived burned-area polygons, not agency perimeters; externalId {firstdate}@{lat},{lon} of the centroid at 2 decimals (the GeoServer ids are rewritten when a polygon grows); observedAt = lastDetected, eventTime = firstDetected; areaHa in hectares; perimeterSource m3. Both: polygons over 9,500 vertices are simplified (geometrySimplified, simplifyToleranceDeg); STANDARD, ALL, no TTL; a perimeter missing from two consecutive complete fetches is tombstoned.

fire-weather.note: Built in 075. cwfis-fwi-stations (CWFIS public:firewx_stns_current, about 1,000 stations): externalId aes (else wmo:{wmo}); when an upper-air and a surface entry share an aes the surface one is kept; name and agency trimmed; observedAt = eventTime = the report time; TTL 36 h from the report time. tempC Cel, rhPct %, windKph and gustKph km/h, windDirDeg deg, precipMm mm, elevationM m; ffmc, dmc, dc, isi, bui, fwi, dsr are the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index System codes.

radio-station.note: Built in 075. radio-browser (Radio Browser directory, mirror discovery restricted to *.api.radio-browser.info): one record per station with a position; externalId stationuuid; observedAt = lastchangetime_iso8601; no geometry for an exact (0,0). name cleaned of control characters; streamUrl, homepage and favicon absolute http(s) links (Foresignal never fetches a stream); tags at most 15; languages as listed; bitrate kbit/s; hls and online booleans, online (the last check succeeded) volatile. Vote, click and check counters are never stored. A station missing from two consecutive complete crawls is tombstoned.

cyclone-cone.note: Built in 075. nhc-cyclone-cones (NOAA NHC_tropical_weather_summary MapServer, layers resolved by name): externalId = stormId, the nhc-cyclones id (basin, two-digit number, year: ep202026); observedAt = the advisory product time (idp_filedate), so a new advisory writes a new version of the same id; advisoryDate is NHC's text. The four cyclone-* kinds are tombstoned per kind once missing from two consecutive complete fetches; out of season every layer is empty. Atlantic, eastern and central Pacific only.

cyclone-track.note: Built in 075. externalId {stormId}:track (records are keyed by source and externalId, so the track cannot share the cone's id); stormId in the payload is the bare nhc-cyclones id.

cyclone-warning.note: Built in 075. One record per coastal watch or warning segment: externalId {stormId}:{tcww}:{n}, n counting the storm's segments of that type from 1 in the layer's object-id order; warningType is the tcww code (TWA tropical storm watch, TWR tropical storm warning, HWA hurricane watch, HWR hurricane warning).

cyclone-forecast-point.note: Built in 075. externalId {stormId}:tau{tau}; eventTime = validTime (validtime DD/HHMM UTC, ISO-8601 in the payload); maxWindKt, gustKt and motionSpeedKt in knots, mslpHpa hPa, motionDirDeg degrees; NHC's 9999 placeholder (pressure and motion past the first point) is left out.

cve-epss.note: epssBand `very-low|low|medium|high|very-high`; raw EPSS scores are not stored.

malware-url.note: `url` is hostile: fieldSpecs `noLink: true`; never render as a link.

space-weather-scales.note: Single entity `current`: current R, S, G scale values and day 1–3 probabilities (key names per fieldSpecs).

ground-station.note: `satdump-{station}` (049): externalId = the station name; state `idle|tracking|receiving|locked|unknown` (unknown without an apiUrl); az/el rounded to 1° and snrDb to 1 dB, so a version is written only on a state or quantized change; observedAt = the time the /api response was read; geometry = the station point; retention 30 d.

radiosonde.note: 086 extended `local-sonde` (auto_rx) within the same contract: param stationCallsign names the observer (else auto_rx's station), the observer carries freq as frequencyHz, and a summary without datetime uses time (HH:MM:SS UTC on the nearest receive day).

water-observation.note: eccc-hydrometric (079 feature-kit spec) maps STATION_NUMBER/STATION_NAME/LEVEL/DISCHARGE per its spec.

threat-alert.note: Alert types other than air raid (artillery, urban fights, chemical, nuclear).

frontline.note: Single entity `occupied-area` (081): mapDate yyyy-MM-dd; areaKm2 on the WGS84 ellipsoid; areaChangeKm2 against the previous map; observedAt = eventTime = map date 03:00 UTC; geometrySimplified and simplifyToleranceDeg only when a map above 9,500 vertices was simplified.

radio-spot.note: Built in 082. pskreporter-ft8: one record per sender, receiver, frequency (kHz) and time slot; externalId sender|receiver|frequencyHz/1000|flowStartSeconds; eventTime = observedAt = flowStartSeconds; point = the center of the sender's Maidenhead cell, quality.accuracyMeters half its diagonal. Receiver callsign is an Observer (`include=observer`, with frequencyHz and snr), never payload.

sdr-receiver.note: Built in 082. kiwisdr: externalId = the list's id; point from gps; observedAtMode RECEIVED; bandsHz is [low, high] in Hz; online is offline == "no"; users and snr ([all, hf] dB) are volatile. A receiver missing from a list at least half the previous size is tombstoned.

scanner.note: Built in 082. openmhz-systems is blocked by a Cloudflare challenge (2026-10): the source reports BLOCKED_CHALLENGE and stores nothing until OpenMHz admits API clients. If reachable: externalId shortName, point from lat/lng when present, clientCount volatile.

aprs-station.note: Built in 082. externalId = the source call with SSID, or the object or item name (a killed object or item is a tombstone); observedAtMode RECEIVED. Position and status are merged per station. weather holds only the values present (windDirDeg, windSpeedMs, windGustMs, tempC, rainLastHourMm, rain24hMm, rainDailyMm, rh, pressureHpa); micEMessage only for Mic-E; sender only for objects and items; path and raw (the TNC2 line, at most 512 characters) are volatile. The igate (aprs-is) or the operator's station (local-aprs) is an Observer (`include=observer`), never payload.

aprs-message.note: Built in 082. Only with `includeMessages=true`; never embedded; acknowledgements and rejections are never stored. externalId FROM>ADDRESSEE{msgId (a text hash when there is no id); path and raw volatile.

mesh-node.note: Built in 083. externalId `!` + 8 hex (Meshtastic node number, unsigned) or `mc:` + the first 12 hex characters of the MeshCore public key. One merged snapshot per node (nodeinfo, position, telemetry); geometry is the last known position, null when never shared, with quality.accuracyMeters from positionPrecisionBits. batteryLevel, voltage, channelUtil, airUtilTx, uptimeS, lastHeardAt, lastAdvertAt and advertTimestamp are volatile; lowBattery (batteryLevel < 15) and advertStatus (MeshCore repeaters: ok, late or silent from the advert age) are significant. hwModel is the hardware name when the source knows it (meshtastic-map, MeshCore device info), else the Meshtastic model number as text; role is the Meshtastic role name. The receiving gateway or own node is an observer (include=observer).

mesh-message.note: Built in 083. Persisted only with `includeText=true`; never embedded or sent to an LLM. externalId `{fromId}:{packetId}` (Meshtastic) or `{fromId | mc:ch{index}}:{senderTimestamp}:{hash}` (MeshCore). channelIndex is absent for a direct message, toId for a broadcast; MeshCore channel messages carry no fromId (the firmware does not say). RSSI and SNR are on the observer.

field-report.note: Built in 084. Private built-in PUSH source written by the mesh channels' report service from `#E R <TYPE> [lat,lon | @place] <text>`; type FIRE|SMOKE|FLOOD|POWER|ROAD|MED|WX|SEC|OTHER, text at most 200 characters (untrusted: never embedded, quoted only as data), reporter is the sender id, channel the private channel index. RECEIVED times; geometry from the coordinates or the place's point; the reporting node is the observer with its RSSI and SNR. externalId `r-` + 16 hex.

acars-message.note: Built in 086. Metadata only: message text is never stored, logged, embedded or forwarded (no parameter enables it); private by descriptor (egress LOCAL_ONLY, not overridable). externalId `protocol|station|epochMillis|tail|msgNum`; eventTime = observedAt = the decoder's time; geometry only from a decoded HFDL position report; the station is the observer with the receive frequency. Kept 7 days.

gnss-integrity.note: Built in 086. integrityState `OK|DEGRADED|JAMMED|SUSPECT_SPOOF|LOST` (significant), judged per 30 s window against a 15-minute baseline of OK windows; the measurements are volatile except mode, uSat, nSat, hdop and eph, which gnss-fix already declares. externalId = the gpsd device, observedAt = the window's last TPV time; geometry = the fix rounded to 2 decimals. local-gpsd-{n} stays private. Kept 30 days.

drone.note: Built in 086. ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN Remote ID from DragonSync's MQTT drone topics only (<root>/drones, <root>/drone/<id>); DJI DroneID detections are dropped (foresignal.remoteid.dropped{reason=dji}). Pilot and home positions are stripped before the record is built; `operatorPoint` {lat, lon} only with `keepOperatorPosition` on a private source (400 PRIVATE_REQUIRED otherwise), never geometry. externalId `rid:<id>`, observedAt = DragonSync `observed_at`; the kit (`seen_by`) is the observer with RSSI and frequency. TRACK, SAMPLED {5 s, keyframe 60 s, 25 m, edge 2 s}, TTL 3 min.

seismic-trigger.note: Built in 086 as the `rsudp-alarm` mapping preset: rsudp's custom module posts {event ALARM|RESET, time, station, channel} to the `mapping` format; externalId `station.channel`, observedAt = eventTime = time, geometry = the custom source's station point.

same-alert.note: Built in 086 (`same` ingest format). externalId `sender|issue|event` (issue as ISO-8601 UTC minutes); eventTime = observedAt = issue (Julian day and UTC time, year from the receive clock with rollover); validUntil = issue + purge (asserted by the sender); geometry = the union of the 040 county polygons (the state's counties for county 000); eventName from the bundled NWS SAME event-code table.

airspace-restriction.note: Built in 087 (faa-tfr). One record per TFR of tfr.faa.gov's exportTfrList: externalId = notam_id (6/8784), observedAt = XNOTAM dateIssued, validFrom = dateEffective, validUntil = dateExpire (upstream-asserted; null means until further notice). XNOTAM times are UTC whatever codeTimeZone says (codeTimeZone names the zone the NOTAM text quotes). Geometry: each area's abdMergedArea (else its Abd parts) with arcs (CWA/CCA) densified at most 2 degrees apart and a lone circle (CIR) as 64 vertices; several areas are a MultiPolygon. lowerFt/upperFt are the lowest floor and highest ceiling of the areas in feet (FL values times 100); lowerRef/upperRef are the XNOTAM codes SFC, ALT (MSL) or HEI (above ground). tfrType, facility and state come from the list, city and regulation (the 14 CFR section, for example 91.137(a)(1)) from the detail; description is the NOTAM text (txtDescrTraditional, untrusted). A TFR that leaves the list is tombstoned.

airport-delay.note: Built in 087 (faa-nas-status, an XML document). externalId ARPT|delayKind; delayKind ground-delay, ground-stop, arrival-delay, departure-delay, general-delay, closure, deicing (other blocks: the block name in kebab case); avgMin/maxMin/minMin are minutes; endTime is a ground stop's end as published (7:45 pm EDT); reopen is a closure's reopening, ISO-8601 UTC from the closure NOTAM's validity or the Reopen text, else as published. observedAt = Update_Time; geometry = the airport's point from the bundled OurAirports table (none for an unknown identifier). A cleared program is tombstoned.

aviation-hazard.note: Built in 087. awc-sigmets (US airsigmet: product SIGMET, AIRMET or OUTLOOK as published; international isigmet: ISIGMET), awc-gairmets (GAIRMET snapshots) and awc-cwas (CWA). externalId icaoId:seriesId:validTimeFrom (isigmet firId:seriesId:validTimeFrom; G-AIRMET product:tag:hazard:validTime:forecast, plus :level for a freezing-level contour, whose pieces are merged; CWA cwsu:seriesId:validTimeFrom). validFrom/validUntil = validTimeFrom/validTimeTo (a G-AIRMET has validFrom = validTime and ends by its 3-hour TTL). baseFt/topFt in feet (G-AIRMET levels are hundreds of feet times 100; a freezing-level contour's level is baseFt); movementDir in degrees (a compass point is converted); qualifier is the G-AIRMET dueTo text for G-AIRMETs. raw is upstream text (untrusted). An advisory missing from the next complete response is tombstoned.

pirep.note: Built in 087 (awc-pireps). externalId receiptTime:lat:lon:sha1(rawOb)[0..8]; eventTime = observedAt = obsTime; fltLvl in hundreds of feet; turbulence and icing are intensity and type (MOD CHOP); skyCover the reported cloud covers in order; reportType PIREP, Urgent PIREP or AIREP; raw is upstream text (untrusted). TTL 2 h on the observation time.

taf.note: Built in 087. One record per station (the newest issue): observedAt = issue time, validFrom/validUntil = the TAF validity (asserted). raw is the TAF text (untrusted); name only from the TAF API (station allowlist), not from the cache file (scope).

uas-facility-cell.note: Built in 087 (faa-uasfm, the FAA_UAS_FacilityMap_Data layer). externalId GLOBALID; observedAt = LAST_EDIT (a M/d/yyyy text date, UTC midnight); ceilingFt in feet above ground; airports the FAA identifiers APT1..5_FAAID; laanc true when any is LAANC-enabled; mapEffective ISO date. The bbox parameter is required.

uas-restriction.note: Built in 087 as feature-kit specs (kits/features/faa-uas.json). faa-uas-nsufr and -parttime carry name (Base), facility, reason, state, floorFt (Surface is 0) and ceilingFt (the AGL ceilings published as text, for example 400' AGL; MSL ceilings are left out) and objectId, their id (no GlobalID; OBJECTID may change when the layer is republished); stadiums, prohibited areas and defense TFR areas carry name, city, state and globalId (GLOBAL_ID), prohibited areas also floorFt/ceilingFt from LOWER_VAL/UPPER_VAL. restrictionType is a constant per source: national-security, national-security-part-time, stadium, prohibited-area, national-defense-tfr.

uas-site.note: Built in 087 (faa-uas-recreational-sites, a feature-kit spec). name SITE_NAME, facility SITE_ID, city, state, ceilingFt (feet), globalId GLOBALID (the id), restrictionType recreational-fixed-site.

maritime-warning.note: Built in 088 (nga-msi-warnings, NGA broadcast-warn?status=active). externalId navArea/msgYear/msgNumber (4/2024/517; navArea P HYDROPAC, A HYDROLANT, C HYDROARC, 4 NAVAREA IV, 12 NAVAREA XII); observedAt = issueDate (DDHHMMZ MON YYYY, UTC). Geometry is recovered from the text: an area BOUNDED BY / BOUND BY at least 3 positions is a Polygon (lettered areas a MultiPolygon), WITHIN n MILES/NM/METERS OF a position a 64-vertex geodesic circle, a TRACKLINE or BETWEEN ... AND ... a LineString (lettered tracklines a MultiLineString), otherwise the positions as a Point or MultiPoint; geometryFromText is false when the text holds no usable position (no geometry). title is the first line of the text (at most 120 characters); text is NGA's text, untrusted, at most 8,000 characters; cancels lists the warnings the text cancels as externalIds. A warning that leaves the active list is tombstoned.

chokepoint-transit.note: Built in 088 (imf-portwatch-chokepoints: IMF PortWatch Daily_Chokepoints_Data joined to PortWatch_chokepoints_database). One record per chokepoint and day: externalId portid:YYYY-MM-DD (chokepoint1:2026-10-03), eventTime = observedAt = the day (UTC midnight), geometry the chokepoint point; n* are vessel transit counts, capacityTotal and capacityTanker deadweight tonnes; rankField nTotal. The data updates weekly with a lag of about ten days.

port.note: imf-portwatch-ports built in 088 (PortWatch_ports_database): externalId portid; observedAt = the layer's edit date (its publication time, since the source's time base is upstream); industries lists industry_top1..3; a port missing from a complete catalog read is tombstoned. world-port-index is a later prompt.

port-activity.note: Built in 088 (imf-portwatch-ports, Daily_Ports_Data). One record per port and day: externalId portid:YYYY-MM-DD, eventTime = observedAt = the day, geometry the port point; importTonnes and exportTonnes are PortWatch's estimated volumes in metric tonnes.

port-disruption.note: Built in 088 as a feature-kit spec (kits/features/imf-portwatch.json, portwatch_disruptions_database). externalId eventid; polygon geometry; validFrom = fromdate, validUntil = todate when set (an open disruption has none); name is eventname; affectedPorts is the upstream's list of PortWatch port ids as text; the HTML description is not stored. observedAt is the time of receipt; a disruption missing from two consecutive complete fetches is tombstoned.

fishing-event.note: Built in 088 (gfw-events, GFW Events API v3, dataset public-global-fishing-events:latest). License CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). externalId the event id; eventTime = start, observedAt = end (else start); start and end are the interval fields; mmsi is GFW's ssvid; durationH is end minus start in hours; distanceKm is the event's totalDistanceKm.

vessel-encounter.note: Built in 088 (gfw-events, public-global-encounters-events:latest; CC BY-NC 4.0). encounterMmsi is the other vessel's ssvid; no distanceKm.

loitering-event.note: Built in 088 (gfw-events, public-global-loitering-events:latest; CC BY-NC 4.0). distanceKm is loitering.totalDistanceKm.

port-visit.note: Built in 088 (gfw-events, public-global-port-visits-events:latest; CC BY-NC 4.0). portName is the visit's start anchorage name (else the intermediate, else the end anchorage); no distanceKm.

sar-vessel-detection.note: Not built in 088. Global Fishing Watch publishes SAR vessel detections (public-global-sar-presence) only as gridded 4Wings data (reports, tiles, bins, cell interaction) without individual detection ids or positions; no official endpoint returns individual detections, so gfw-sar-detections is not implemented (Source Catalog).

notice-to-mariners.note: Not built in 088. NAVCEN's Local Notice to Mariners application links GeoJSON files by notice category (hazNav_1.geojson, marEvent_1.geojson, tmpChange_1.geojson, ...), chunked by a counter in fileIndexNew.json and not split by district, with no API documentation; the prompt requires a documented, stable per-district download, so uscg-lnm-* is a planned Source Catalog row.

cap-alert.note: Built in 089 (the reviewed cap-* family from the WMO Register of Alerting Authorities, and the meteoalarm-* family). externalId is the root identifier of the shared update chain (CapThreadResolver); an Update versions the same record and a Cancel is a tombstone of the thread. observedAt=sent, eventTime=onset, validFrom=onset ?? effective, validUntil=expires. Geometry is the union of polygon/circle areas, or null with geometryFromGeocode=false for a geocode-only area. headline/description are capped at 4 KB and instruction at 2 KB; headline and description are embedded (untrusted). entityKeys cap-identifier. A non-Actual status is skipped unless includeTests is set.

rainfall-outlook.note: Built in 089 (the five WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook feature-kit sources, kits/features/wpc-ero.json). category is 1–4 = MRGL/SLGT/MDT/HIGH (upstream dn). observedAt=issue_time, validFrom=start_time, validUntil=end_time, read as UTC. Absence tombstones.

shakemap-mmi.note: Built in 089 (usgs-shakemap). externalId `{eventId}:mmi{level}`; geometry is a MultiLineString contour of one MMI level, simplified with TopologyPreservingSimplifier to at most 10,000 vertices. A level that disappears in a newer shakemap version is tombstoned.

natural-event.note: Built in 090 (nasa-eonet). The latest geometry entry is the record geometry; the response is JSON despite its RSS content type.

displacement.note: Numeric payload; upstream key names, absent for `-`.

sanction.note: Built in 091 (ofac-sdn with the legacy SDN.XML/CONS_PRIM.XML export, uk-sanctions-list from the FCDO list that replaced the closed OFSI list, un-sanctions from the UN consolidated XML). list `SDN|OFAC-CONS|UK|UN`; partyType `individual|entity|vessel|aircraft`; no geometry. entityKeys imo, mmsi, registration (from aircraftTail, since 098), un-reference. A delisting is a tombstone unless the list shrank below 90% (LIST_SHRINK_GUARD; POST /v1/sources/{sourceId}/fetch?allowShrink=true accepts it). designationSource and sanctionsImposed are UK only (split on |).

filing.note: Built in 091 (sec-8k). externalId is the accession number; item codes (e.g. 1.05) come from the summary. The SEC requires a declared User-Agent with contact details.

bgp-hijack.note: Upstream snake_case keys kept as the prompt specifies.

service-incident.note: status-aws and status-azure arrive through the 073 feed kit with bulletin-style keys.

satellite-scene.note: Links only; Foresignal never fetches imagery.

nws-alert.note: externalId = properties.id; observedAt = sent, eventTime = onset ?? effective, validFrom = onset, validUntil = the later of expires and ends. Geometry: the polygon, else the ref_admin2 county union for county-only UGCs (geometrySource county-union), else none. description and instruction are untrusted upstream text (≤ 8 KB). Authoritative.

example.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 12 at 6:42PM CDT until October 12 at 7:15PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
example.description: At 642 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado was located ...
example.instruction: TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building.

probsevere-object.note: externalId = ProbSevere ID; observedAt = the file's validTime; objects inside the places-AOI envelope only; tombstoned when absent from the newest processed file. muCape, mlCape, ebShearKt, srh01km and flashRate are volatile. Automated guidance, never a warning.

spc-outlook.note: externalId = day{d}:{type}:{LABEL} (day1:cat:MDT, day1:torn:0.10, day1:sigtorn:SIGN); observedAt = ISSUE, eventTime = VALID, validUntil = EXPIRE. dn is SPC's rank (categorical TSTM 2, MRGL 3, SLGT 4, ENH 5, MDT 6, HIGH 8). Labels absent from a re-fetched layer are tombstoned for that day and type.

metar.note: externalId = station id; observedAt = eventTime = observation_time; TTL 3 h anchored on the observation. Reused by 087 (TAF, PIREP, G-AIRMET).

lightning-cluster.note: externalId = lc-{ulid}, carried to the nearest cluster within 15 km between GLM files; DBSCAN (eps 8 km haversine, minPts 3) over the places-AOI ring's last 5 minutes. Geometry = centroid Point to 0.01°. observedAt = newest member flash; eventTime = the cluster's first flash. Quantized payload: flashes5m is a bucket lower bound (3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200), radiusKm to 1 km, maxEnergyFj a decade lower bound. Tombstoned after 10 minutes of processed GLM data without members; while the feed is stalled (no file processed for more than 2 minutes) clusters freeze. GLM-only lightning rules should use 15 km or more; all-clears are advisory.

fire-cluster.note: externalId = fc-{ulid}, carried between processed scans by the largest pixel overlap. Members: the 8-connected components of the FDC detections after a 1-pixel dilation. Geometry = convex hull of member pixel centers buffered 1 km, vertices to 0.01° (a Point for one pixel). observedAt = scan start; eventTime = first sighting. Tombstoned after 3 processed scans without members.

smoke-polygon.note: NOAA HMS analyst smoke polygon. externalId = first 16 hex characters of sha256(date|start|end|density|satellite|centroid to 0.1°). eventTime = Start, observedAt = End, TTL 24 h anchored on observedAt. Ids absent from a complete, successfully fetched file are tombstoned (analyst edits).

place-weather.note: externalId = place:{placeId}; one record per place, written only when the quantized payload changes (no heartbeat versions); no geometry (a place's position is sensitive). Each section (radar, hail, precip, lightning, cell, smoke, forecast.gfs) has status ok|stale|no-coverage|unavailable: when its input is older than maxGap (MRMS 6 min, GLM 2 min), comes from a failing source or lacks coverage, it keeps its previous values, sets the status and adds asOf (time of the last good data, fixed while not ok); before the first good data a section carries its status only. 999 = none within 100 km (and no approaching core for cell.eta50Min). Distances to 0.5 km below 10 km else 1 km, ETAs to 5 min, rates to 1 mm/h, dBZ to 0.5. radar.nearest50Km10m and lightning.nearestKm30m are rolling minimums. Verified-clear helpers radar.verifiedNearest50Km10m and lightning.verifiedNearestKm30m equal the metric while the section is ok and 0 otherwise, so `<= X` on them is true when near or unknown (use them for all-clear exit rules). GLM's footprint over Texas is about 8–10 km and its detection efficiency below 100%: GLM-only rules should use 15 km or more; all-clears are advisory. Tombstoned when the place is deleted (which can fire exit rules), never because input is stale. Automated guidance, never a warning. Prompt 053: precip adds qpe1hMmMax, qpe24hMmMax and ffgRatio1hPctMax (maxima within the radius, whole units); each input keeps the section rules on its own, and precip.status is the worst of the rate and of the inputs that have had data. forecast.nws = {status, popMax24h, qpf24hMm, gustMaxMs24h} from the place's nws-forecast head: stale when its forecastUpdated is older than 6 h, unavailable while nws-gridpoints is disabled or failing or has no forecast for the place. Prompt 105: forecast.ifs = {status, gustMax24h, precip24hMm} from the IFS run; forecast.disagreement = {fields, spread, models} when GFS, HRRR (within its 18 h run) and IFS spread over the next 24 h exceeds the thresholds (gust 8 m/s, precipitation max(15 mm, half the mean), 2 m temperature 4 K), with hysteresis clearing at 75% of the threshold.

wx-area.note: externalId = {field}:{threshold}:{aoi} (field refl, mesh, precip, or from 053 rotation, qpe1h or ffg; aoi a place id or `aoi`), from the `areas` parameter (default refl:50:aoi, mesh:25:aoi), computed every 6–10 min (param `interval`, default 8 min). areaKm2 to 2 significant figures, maxValue to 0.5 dBZ (refl) or whole units, coveragePct an integer. Geometry = the thresholded mask polygons simplified and snapped to about 1 km, null when nothing reaches the threshold. Stale, failing or uncovered input keeps the previous values (geometry included) with a non-ok status and asOf. Tombstoned when its place is deleted or it leaves the `areas` parameter.

radar-cell.note: externalId = c-{ulid}. Per MRMS reflectivity frame inside the places AOI (scope=conus on the large profile): 40 dBZ mask, 3×3 opening, 8-connected union-find labeling, split at 50 dBZ cores, run-rectangle union to polygons snapped to about 500 m. maxDbz to 0.5, areaKm2 to 2 significant figures, meshMax whole mm (omitted without a current MESH frame), glmFlashes5m a bucket lower bound (0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200). motion (centroid-v1): nearest-centroid match to the previous frame within 30 km per 10 min of gap, least squares over the last 3 matches; speedKmh to 5, bearingDeg (direction of travel) to 10°. observedAt = frame valid time; eventTime = first seen. Unmatched cells get new ids; cells absent from a processed frame are tombstoned (a stale or missing frame tombstones nothing).

nws-forecast.note: externalId = place:{placeId}; one record per selected place (all places, or those with product `nws` when allPlaces=false; at most maxPlaces, default 50). observedAt = the forecast's updateTime (UPSTREAM); no eventTime, no TTL, no geometry (a place's position is sensitive). The 24-hour summaries cover the first 24 hours from the fetch hour of the hourly expansion of the gridpoint layers (accumulations divided evenly over their intervals; wind in m/s). hazards: at most 10, type = phenomenon.significance. Fetched hourly per place with If-Modified-Since; a 304 or a failed request keeps the record. The 72-hour hourly series is cached in forecast_series_cache (provider nws) and served as ForecastSeries by getPlaceWeather and weather_forecast. Tombstoned when the place is deleted or leaves the selection.

storm-report.note: externalId = the first 12 hex of SHA-256 over type|convDate|HHMM|lat|lon|location (reports have no upstream id). observedAt = eventTime = the report time: HHMM UTC within the SPC convective day (12 UTC to 12 UTC; rows before 1200 fall on the next calendar date). Point geometry. From today.csv every 10 minutes and yesterday.csv hourly (conditional GETs; three CSV sections: tornado F_Scale, wind Speed in mph, hail Size in hundredths of an inch). magnitude is omitted for UNK. comments are untrusted upstream text (≤ 500 chars). Never tombstoned on absence; no TTL.

forecast-area.note: externalId = {model}:{field}:{op}{value}:{aoi} (e.g. ifs:gust:>=25:aoi), from the wx-forecast-areas `thresholds` parameter (product:op:value[:horizonHours], horizon at most 120 h). Per completed model run (GFS, HRRR, IFS), the polygon where the field is forecast to cross the threshold inside the places AOI: per-step masks unioned, 3x3 opening, run-rectangle union, simplified at 0.02 deg. validFrom = the first exceeding valid time; validUntil = the last exceeding valid time plus the step. areaKm2 to 2 significant figures; peakValue/peakAt quantised. Emitted only on a change of the quantised payload or of the geometry (symmetric difference over 10%); tombstoned when the exceedance disappears in a newer run. Automated, not a warning.

storm-track.note: externalId = t-{ulid}.
